WeUNn9rlIi.one_liner: Zero-shot RL with Gaussian-regularized latent-dynamics successor features and test-time search over the pretrained policy family.
WeUNn9rlIi.problem: Successor-feature zero-shot RL overlooks how representation geometry affects SF evaluation, and direct policy retrieval can be suboptimal under reward misspecification and function-approximation errors.
WeUNn9rlIi.method: GLDSF combines latent dynamics prediction with regularization toward an isotropic Gaussian to learn well-conditioned control-relevant representations. A model-based test-time adjustment then searches over the pretrained policy family rather than action sequences, with no parameter updates or extra environment interaction.
WeUNn9rlIi.key_idea: Regularize latent successor features toward an isotropic Gaussian for well-conditioned evaluation, then search over pretrained policy codes with a learned model at test time.
WeUNn9rlIi.evidence: ExORL benchmark with state and pixel inputs, ablation studies, and an analysis supporting the adjustment design.
WeUNn9rlIi.claimed_gains: Planning-free GLDSF outperforms the strongest pixel baseline by 24.0% in aggregate and is competitive with the strongest state-based baseline, and test-time adjustment adds 7.1% on states and 8.4% on pixels.
WeUNn9rlIi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is well motivated by prior work and theory, separates the reward coefficient from the behavior code, and gives clean evidence that Gaussian regularization helps on pixels plus a clever test-time adjustment.
WeUNn9rlIi.main_concern: Only minor points are raised, such as a missing reproducibility statement and an overstated connection to skill composition.

AwJ9Lw5Pld.one_liner: Cross-domain benchmark of 26 expert-verified tasks that scores agents on discovered mechanisms and the insights they support.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.problem: Current benchmarks do not test whether AI agents can turn long-horizon experiments into mechanisms and scientific insights rather than only optimizing predictive accuracy.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.method: EurekaBench provides 26 long-horizon tasks across neuroscience, computer science, chemistry, astrophysics, geophysics, and plasma physics, with 306 insights expected to follow from the discovered mechanism. The evaluation separates predictive accuracy from scientific insight, and judge agents decide which insights a submitted mechanism supports.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.key_idea: Score a discovered mechanism by how many expected insights it supports, as decided by judge agents, separately from its predictive accuracy on the data.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.evidence: An expert-verified set of 26 tasks across six domains with 306 insights, evaluated with comparisons against human reference solutions.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and that separating predictive accuracy from scientific insight, with domain experts selecting problems and checking insight questions, is a valuable benchmark design.
AwJ9Lw5Pld.main_concern: The insight scores rely on LLM judges whose verdicts are not validated per insight against humans, raising reliability and self-preference concerns, and the private evaluation data and rubrics limit reproducibility.

1nVm6m48DD.one_liner: Per-query router jointly choosing model, scaling strategy, and test-time scaling graph under an average compute budget
1nVm6m48DD.problem: Existing test-time scaling allocates compute per task with a single TTS graph, overlooking large per-query variation in compute needs.
1nVm6m48DD.method: A budget-aware TTS-Router estimates per-action success probabilities and selects actions by Lagrangian optimization, while a training-free TTS-Planner builds the TTS graph on the fly from verifier feedback, using low-cost probe responses to improve routing reliability.
1nVm6m48DD.key_idea: Predict per-action success probabilities from probe responses and verifier feedback, select actions via Lagrangian budget allocation, and grow the TTS graph at runtime from verifier feedback.
1nVm6m48DD.evidence: Experiments on three datasets with a weak-to-strong LLM pool and multiple budget settings, plus analyses of monetary budgets and out-of-distribution queries; the paper claims the strongest performance-cost trade-off among compared methods.
1nVm6m48DD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the query-adaptive routing setting practical and the design supported by clear experiments, with good performance-cost trade-offs across budget settings.
1nVm6m48DD.main_concern: Theoretical support is thin: the planner's verifier-guided rules lack formal analysis, and Proposition 1 does not explain why success-probability prediction beats direct oracle prediction.

YDa8hCw653.one_liner: Analyzes MeanFlow and Lagrangian flow-map losses as functional gradient flows to explain stop-gradient and adaptive weighting.
YDa8hCw653.problem: Stop-gradient operators and adaptive weighting are crucial in flow-map training, but their effect on the training dynamics has not been analyzed.
YDa8hCw653.method: Analyzes the functional gradient flow induced by the MeanFlow and Lagrangian losses and proves convergence to the true flow map, shows finite updates can be unbounded, and shows adaptive normalization gives bounded updates and, with a specific weighting, convergence to a neighborhood of the solution.
YDa8hCw653.key_idea: Treat flow-map training as a functional gradient flow, showing adaptive normalization bounds otherwise possibly unbounded updates and, with specific weighting, yields convergence to a neighborhood of the solution.
YDa8hCw653.evidence: Theory (including Theorem 4 under a linear-growth residual assumption) plus synthetic-data experiments testing the gradient-flow analysis, with generation quality reported by FID per reviews.
YDa8hCw653.claimed_gains: not stated; theoretical results only (convergence of MeanFlow and Lagrangian losses to the true flow map, bounded updates under adaptive normalization).
YDa8hCw653.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis rigorous and interpretable, giving a theoretical lens on stop-gradient and adaptive weighting, with experiments that complement the theory.
YDa8hCw653.main_concern: Experiments emphasize FID rather than direct stability evidence such as gradient norms, and Theorem 4 relies on an assumption that the squared residual grows at most linearly whose practical validity is unclear.

mFld0i4oyi.one_liner: Abstracts a single human video into sequential scene graphs that generate reset states and dense stage rewards for dexterous RL.
mFld0i4oyi.problem: Imitating motions from one human video limits generalization to new object poses, goals and grasps, while unguided RL struggles to explore high-dimensional multi-stage tasks.
mFld0i4oyi.method: Dex-One2Many converts the video into stage-wise scene graphs that act as generative constraints for sampling diverse reset states and provide dense rewards per stage. Policies train entirely in simulation and transfer zero-shot to a real multi-fingered hand.
mFld0i4oyi.key_idea: Constrain object relations rather than exact poses in stage-wise scene graphs, and use them to sample varied reset states and give dense per-stage rewards for RL.
mFld0i4oyi.evidence: Five tool-use and manipulation tasks with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer to a multi-fingered hand; baselines per reviews mainly rely on motion imitation.
mFld0i4oyi.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before its results.
mFld0i4oyi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of extracting stage-wise scene-graph task structure instead of imitating motion original and well motivated, with compelling real-world results.
mFld0i4oyi.main_concern: Baselines are insufficient (no goal-conditioned RL with the same rewards, resets and training budget), generalization is overstated since it covers new configurations but not new tasks or scenes, and compute is heavy.

TJteJVAzk1.one_liner: RoboBranch runs multiple candidate actions from identical simulator states and revises task guidance from all outcomes for frozen robot-use agents.
TJteJVAzk1.problem: Robot-use agents learn from independent rollouts that reveal one outcome per visited state, so testing another action means reaching a state that differs in both context and action.
TJteJVAzk1.method: Shared-State Branching executes several candidate actions from identical copies of each decision state, Outcome-Grounded Guidance Learning revises task guidance from every outcome, and Width-Scalable Runtime proposes all candidates in one response and runs branches in parallel.
TJteJVAzk1.key_idea: Branch from copies of the same simulator state to compare outcomes of different actions, then rewrite task guidance from all successful and failed outcomes.
TJteJVAzk1.evidence: LIBERO-Pro, RoboCasa365 and RoboTwin C2R against Harness VLA built on the same open-source Qwen model, with compute-matched independent-rollout comparisons and an efficiency analysis per reviews.
TJteJVAzk1.claimed_gains: RoboBranch improves over Harness VLA built on the same open-source Qwen model by 10.6 (the unit and further figures are cut off in the abstract).
TJteJVAzk1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, sound and clearly presented, and that compute-matched comparisons support gains from branching beyond extra rollouts.
TJteJVAzk1.main_concern: Novelty over prior branching and execution-feedback methods such as ASPIRE is not isolated, and snapshot-based branching applies only to simulation.

YD3P9EI37h.one_liner: OLMo-Detect: membership-inference benchmark across pre-, mid- and post-training, with aligned members and non-members filtered by 13-gram overlap.
YD3P9EI37h.problem: Existing membership-inference benchmarks cover few training stages, align members and non-members poorly, and do not rigorously filter non-members against the training corpus.
YD3P9EI37h.method: Builds the benchmark on the fully open OLMo 2 pipeline across pre-training, mid-training and post-training, aligns members and non-members on three axes (text quality, temporal range, lexical statistics), filters non-members via infini-gram, and adds a Shifted variant with misaligned members.
YD3P9EI37h.key_idea: Members and non-members are matched on text quality, temporal range and lexical similarity, and non-members are filtered against the full training corpus using infini-gram n-gram overlap.
YD3P9EI37h.evidence: Evaluation of 15 unsupervised and 3 supervised membership inference attacks across the OLMo 2 family, including cross-domain and shifted-distribution tests.
YD3P9EI37h.claimed_gains: No improvement is claimed; the best unsupervised and supervised attacks both reach an AUC of only 0.68.
YD3P9EI37h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully constructed, spans all three training stages including mid-training, controls for distribution shift, and is reproducible.
YD3P9EI37h.main_concern: Filtering thresholds (13-gram, 20% overlap) are not ablated, the findings are only partly new relative to MIMIR, and possible GSM8K leakage across mid- and post-training confounds the stage comparison.

HT2l0P1E04.one_liner: Discrete diffusion whose noisy state is a set of candidate tokens per position, changed by gradual additions and removals.
HT2l0P1E04.problem: Masked and uniform diffusion erase a token's identity in a single corruption event, so noisy states cannot represent partially resolved uncertainty where several alternatives remain plausible.
HT2l0P1E04.method: A continuous-time discrete diffusion family where each position holds a binary membership vector over tokens and candidate sets change through additions and removals, using a symmetric formulation and a confidence-guided Psi-sampler.
HT2l0P1E04.key_idea: Corrupt each position into a candidate set stored as a binary membership vector, so information is lost and recovered gradually and uncertainty is part of the diffusion state.
HT2l0P1E04.evidence: Sudoku-Extreme, Boxoban and graph coloring against masked and uniform baselines under matched architectures and budgets, plus language modeling on Text8, TinyStories and OpenWebText.
HT2l0P1E04.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong, well-tuned masked and uniform baselines on logic and planning tasks, with the largest gains on the hardest instances, while remaining competitive on language modeling; no numbers stated.
HT2l0P1E04.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is clear, mathematically sound and natural, and that studying the corruption-state representation is a worthwhile direction with promising benchmark results.
HT2l0P1E04.main_concern: Gains may come from the sampler rather than the kernel (on Sudoku the uniform kernel matches or beats binary at shared samplers), experiments are small-scale, and why explicit candidate sets are needed is not justified.

TG38ZQRlH8.one_liner: GrabMe merges ViT tokens on a spatial adjacency graph with one-hop constraints and dynamic-programming candidate selection for segmentation.
TG38ZQRlH8.problem: Global-matching or rigid local-grouping token merging perturbs spatial relationships and degrades fine details, and pairwise similarity alone can blur object boundaries and small objects.
TG38ZQRlH8.method: GrabMe, training-free, constrains merging to one-hop neighbors on a spatial adjacency graph where merged groups inherit adjacencies. Dynamic programming builds a conflict-free maximum-cardinality candidate pool for parallel merging, and one-hop similarity distributions add structural context to the merge decision.
TG38ZQRlH8.key_idea: Merge only one-hop neighbors on a spatial graph, choosing a maximal conflict-free candidate set by dynamic programming and scoring pairs with neighborhood similarity distributions.
TG38ZQRlH8.evidence: Experiments with ViT backbones on semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation benchmarks, with an ablation of DP versus greedy candidate selection.
TG38ZQRlH8.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the results.
TG38ZQRlH8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method well motivated and clearly presented, with thorough results across segmentation tasks and backbones showing a better accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
TG38ZQRlH8.main_concern: Differences from existing local or graph-based merging methods (for example G2TM, DHTM and TRACE's boundary inference) are not clearly established, and why DP selection beats greedy is not fully disentangled.

y76l6Xpmtm.one_liner: Region-flexible weather forecasting with geo-aware position encoding, random regional sampling, and a router that selects relevant global tokens.
y76l6Xpmtm.problem: Data-driven regional forecasters generalize poorly across regions with different locations and extents and struggle to filter relevant global information.
y76l6Xpmtm.method: ARGO combines Geo-aware Position Encoding (GaPE), random regional sampling, and an auxiliary alignment loss to learn transferable forecasting patterns and compatible geographic representations. A Global Token Router selects relevant nearby and remote tokens while retaining broad global context, followed by latent-space cross-attention for regional-global fusion.
y76l6Xpmtm.key_idea: Train on randomly sampled regions with geo-aware positional encoding, and use a router to pick nearby and remote global tokens for cross-attention fusion with the regional model.
y76l6Xpmtm.evidence: Experiments at 0.25 degree resolution (ERA5 per reviews) comparing regional forecasting against baselines, plus a held-out region generalization test.
y76l6Xpmtm.claimed_gains: Outperforms the baselines in regional forecasting and generalizes across regions without retraining from scratch; no figures stated.
y76l6Xpmtm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the region-reuse problem useful and see promising improvements over the evaluated baselines and a held-out-region experiment on ERA5 data.
y76l6Xpmtm.main_concern: Region flexibility is validated only on one fixed East Asian window with a single held-out region, and ablations do not isolate GaPE or the alignment loss.

vamTQUI0qS.one_liner: Information-theoretic analysis and blind-corrected probes test whether emergent social learning in artificial agents comes with modelling of the expert.
vamTQUI0qS.problem: It is unclear how emergent social learning in artificial agents relates to expert modelling, since encoding observations of an expert need not amount to modelling that expert.
vamTQUI0qS.method: The paper shows information-theoretically that social learning requires encoding the expert's observations but not necessarily modelling the expert, and designs blind-corrected probes that compare what can be decoded about the expert from the learner's representation against an expert-masked baseline. Three hypotheses linking social learning and expert modelling are tested across four environments.
vamTQUI0qS.key_idea: Blind-corrected probes subtract an expert-masked decoding baseline from probe scores to measure how much of a learner's expert encoding is genuine expert modelling.
vamTQUI0qS.evidence: Four environments (GoalCycle, Overcooked, Brax Ant, Travelling Salesman) testing three hypotheses, with controlled experiments such as revealing the latent goal and a misaligned GoalCycle setup.
vamTQUI0qS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the information-theoretic framework and blind-corrected probes well motivated, with a clear three-hypothesis structure and evaluation across four distinct environments.
vamTQUI0qS.main_concern: The main text is clunky in places with wide confidence intervals in some experiments, and one reviewer asks how the measured expert modelling differs from task-relevant information inferred through observation.

w1qlNX8tP2.one_liner: Cross-fitted estimator of CDF-based distributional treatment effects that combines surrogate scores with a small subsample of observed primary outcomes.
w1qlNX8tP2.problem: Estimating a treatment's effect on the outcome distribution is hard when a surrogate outcome is observed for everyone but the primary outcome only for a subsample, as in LLM evaluation with automated judges and few human ratings.
w1qlNX8tP2.method: Building on prediction-powered inference and surrogate-assisted treatment-effect estimation, the estimator combines cross-fitted conditional CDFs with and without surrogate information. The paper derives a Gaussian-process limit, uniform confidence bands over outcome thresholds, and the semiparametric efficiency bound.
w1qlNX8tP2.key_idea: Combine cross-fitted conditional CDFs with and without surrogate information in a semiparametrically efficient estimator that needs no agreement between surrogate and primary scales.
w1qlNX8tP2.evidence: Theory (Gaussian-process limit, uniform bands, efficiency bound), simulations, and four real data applications spanning LLM evaluation, natural language, and clinical trials per reviews.
w1qlNX8tP2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem timely for LLM evaluation, the semiparametric theory rigorous, and the method useful because it needs no shared scale between surrogate and primary outcomes.
w1qlNX8tP2.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because the setting and efficiency results follow existing surrogate-assisted and doubly robust work, and empirical gains over PPI++ are modest.

1eTpxVIxA1.one_liner: Corrects person-suppressed MLLM predictions for cultural attribution by contrasting original and person-focused views of the same image, training-free.
1eTpxVIxA1.problem: MLLMs assign different cultural origins to the same content depending on the people depicted, and suppressing person cues alone can hide relevant cultural evidence while leaving attribution errors.
1eTpxVIxA1.method: TVMCC uses task-aware masking to produce a person-suppressed view and a complementary person-focused view of the same image. It then revises the suppressed ranking by contrasting candidate preferences in the original and person-focused views, with no additional training or test labels.
1eTpxVIxA1.key_idea: Build the correction reference from the same image by contrasting original and person-focused views, then use it to revise the person-suppressed candidate ranking.
1eTpxVIxA1.evidence: Six MLLMs on Cultural Counterfactuals and MixCuBe (18 model-task settings), plus a reference-shuffling control with matched correction magnitudes.
1eTpxVIxA1.claimed_gains: Outperforms original-image predictions in all 18 model-task settings and achieves the highest reported accuracy in 17; nationality attribution gains on Cultural Counterfactuals range from 10.4 to 16.9 percentage points, exceeding person suppression on all six models.
1eTpxVIxA1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free method simple and the evaluation thorough and honest (paired bootstrap CIs, shuffling controls, ablations), with gains across multiple MLLMs.
1eTpxVIxA1.main_concern: One reviewer argues most gains come from suppression and masking rather than the correction itself, which adds only about 0.2-3 points over same-mask suppression with some intervals including zero.

fWZhqCfsio.one_liner: Gated spatial pooler plus a learned granularity router give MLLMs content-adaptive coarse or fine visual tokens.
fWZhqCfsio.problem: MLLMs encode inputs as dense fixed-size patch tokens, while existing pruning and adaptive methods lack content-adaptive granularity, task generalization, and compatibility with modern MLLMs and serving stacks.
fWZhqCfsio.method: A gated spatial pooler builds coarse representations alongside native fine ones in a shared MRoPE coordinate, and a granularity router learns which to use per region. Trained by self-distillation, validated on Qwen3.5-4B and scaled to Qwen3.8-27B with over 30K A100 GPU-hours.
fWZhqCfsio.key_idea: Learn end to end, via self-distillation, a router that chooses between coarse pooled and native fine tokens within one shared positional coordinate system.
fWZhqCfsio.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.8-27B; reviewers cite comparisons with token-pruning baselines such as FastV and serving throughput and latency results at 27B on long video.
fWZhqCfsio.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.8-27B, saves 43.0% of tokens on average while retaining 98.9% native (abstract text truncated).
fWZhqCfsio.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the learnable, deployable design with detailed training and serving information, and the token savings and throughput at 27B scale.
fWZhqCfsio.main_concern: The evidence does not separate the router's contribution from the three-stage distillation and in-domain data, and routing is binary and content-based rather than question-aware.

LvWfC8HCom.one_liner: Adapts a frozen flow-based VLA at test time by learning the mean of its initial-noise source distribution.
LvWfC8HCom.problem: VLA agents are brittle under deployment distribution shifts, though failed rollouts often retain task-directed behavior, suggesting unreliable access to pretrained capabilities rather than their absence.
LvWfC8HCom.method: ReFlowTTA learns the source distribution of initial noise of a flow-based VLA, shifting probability mass toward states tied to better outcomes using task feedback and optional human corrections. The pretrained flow model stays frozen.
LvWfC8HCom.key_idea: Instead of changing how actions are produced, learn where generation starts by optimizing a low-dimensional source-noise mean with task feedback, with human corrections entering via inverse flow.
LvWfC8HCom.evidence: Three simulation benchmarks and two real-world robot platforms against test-time adaptation baselines, with analyses of source-space dimensionality and perturbation directionality.
LvWfC8HCom.claimed_gains: Outperforms representative test-time adaptation methods with limited deployment interactions; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
LvWfC8HCom.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a simple, parameter-efficient adaptation interface for a frozen VLA with consistent gains across simulation and real-robot settings.
LvWfC8HCom.main_concern: Novelty relative to noise-space adaptation work (DSRL, UniSteer, FlowDAgger) is not adequately discussed, and the optimization procedure is under-specified and relies on dense task feedback.

ym9Apmox4B.one_liner: Learns robot video rewards from path bounds combined by a quasimetric, then distills them into a language-conditioned model.
ym9Apmox4B.problem: Temporal-progress reward models measure the demonstrator's value rather than the optimal one, so pauses and detours distort the target and failed attempts yield no target.
ym9Apmox4B.method: QRM treats each video segment as a feasible path whose return lower-bounds the optimal value, and a quasimetric model tightens the estimates through the triangle inequality. It then distills the value of reaching the nearest successful outcome into a compact model conditioned on visual history and language.
ym9Apmox4B.key_idea: Learn from bounds rather than regression targets: segment returns bound optimal value, the quasimetric triangle inequality tightens them, and a language-conditioned model distills nearest-goal value.
ym9Apmox4B.evidence: MetaWorld tasks unseen during reward-model training with imperfect videos, against vision-language reward models; reviewers also cite real-robot experiments on three tasks.
ym9Apmox4B.claimed_gains: Outperforms vision-language reward models 50x its size on unseen MetaWorld tasks with imperfect videos; the remaining numbers are cut off in the abstract.
ym9Apmox4B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framing of progress versus optimal value well motivated, and the use of failed trajectories without outcome labels and the compact distilled model practical.
ym9Apmox4B.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate QRM's contribution: shaping-term effects are unclear, bound-versus-regression gaps show overlapping confidence intervals, and real-robot reward scales differ across methods.

KZt66uKtBy.one_liner: Shows word-substitution attacks bypass safety monitors even when told the mappings, with hidden states separating mappings but safety decisions unchanged
KZt66uKtBy.problem: Word substitution can bypass language-model safeguards, and it is unclear whether external safety monitors recognize harmful content even when told what the substituted words mean.
KZt66uKtBy.method: A systematic empirical study of substitution attacks across seven generation services and seven monitors using paired held-out inputs with explicit meanings restored, plus an open-weight monitor analysis in which codeword meanings are swapped while vocabulary, questions, and answers are fixed, probing hidden states and attention.
KZt66uKtBy.key_idea: Fixing vocabulary, questions, and answers while swapping codeword meanings shows hidden states encode the mapping (linearly separable) yet safety scores stay below threshold.
KZt66uKtBy.evidence: Seven generation services, seven monitors on paired held-out inputs (30 independent questions per reviewers), an open-weight monitor with linear probes and attention analysis, and demonstration and lightweight fine-tuning mitigations.
KZt66uKtBy.claimed_gains: Seven monitors show 13.3-76.7 percentage-point alarm reductions on paired held-out inputs despite explicit meanings, and templates, output prefixes, and general instructions receive 92% of direct decision-position attention.
KZt66uKtBy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired, controlled evaluation convincingly shows that monitors rely on question wording and that substitution bypasses them even with explicit mappings.
KZt66uKtBy.main_concern: Reviewers say the evaluation set is small and dominated by DeepSeek (26 of 30 harmful responses), and the internal analysis shows distinguishability but not why monitors fail, given a possible positional shortcut.

iC2Y5WF0yT.one_liner: A physics engine, not an LLM, decides whether a building design passes, while the LLM only proposes discrete structural revisions
iC2Y5WF0yT.problem: Most agents for automated building design produce visually plausible models without verification grounded in mechanical analysis and seismic and wind code compliance.
iC2Y5WF0yT.method: PE-Loop is a harness in which a deterministic physics engine is the sole source of evaluation signals, mapping code constraints to a physics process reward, while the language model is confined to proposing discrete revisions to section menu, topology, and lateral system. Designs are verified by held-out seismic and wind time-history checks and a detailing check.
iC2Y5WF0yT.key_idea: Give acceptance authority to a deterministic simulator that maps code constraints to a process reward, and restrict the LLM to proposing discrete structural revisions.
iC2Y5WF0yT.evidence: VB-Bench, 3,577 physics-adjudicated building instances across five code families, with four backbone LLMs, held-out seismic and wind checks, an LLM-judge ablation, and rule-based variants with no LLM.
iC2Y5WF0yT.claimed_gains: PE-Loop achieves the highest verified success rate under three of four backbone LLMs, the highest held-out seismic pass rate under all four, and the highest held-out wind pass rate under three; an LLM judge without simulator output leaves 58.43% of accepted designs noncompliant.
iC2Y5WF0yT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is meaningful, the physics-engine-as-judge pipeline and the gap between raw and verified success are valuable evaluation contributions, and the four-backbone evaluation is informative.
iC2Y5WF0yT.main_concern: Reviewers say the experiments do not isolate acceptance authority as the source of reliability, since the LLM-judge baseline also lacks simulator outputs and rule-based variants with no LLM do not differ significantly from PE-Loop.

5IgalfMBKx.one_liner: Pairs declarative Lean postconditions with executable counterparts so test-case agreement serves as a reinforcement-learning reward for specification generation
5IgalfMBKx.problem: Training specification models needs scalable feedback on whether generated specifications capture intended behavior, and prior approaches rely on explicit proofs or separately implemented code with correspondence proofs, both expensive.
5IgalfMBKx.method: AuXSpec pairs each declarative postcondition with an executable counterpart, obtained through type class resolution when possible and otherwise defined separately with an equivalence proof, so test cases evaluate specifications by execution. It synthesizes 3,037 LeetCode problems, expands training to 19.5K samples through expert iteration on Codeforces, and trains Qwen models with the execution-based reward.
5IgalfMBKx.key_idea: Executable counterparts let test-case agreement with a declarative Lean specification act as an RL reward without a proof for each candidate.
5IgalfMBKx.evidence: Training Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B on a synthesized corpus, evaluated on AuXSpec-Test and the out-of-domain Verina benchmark against frontier models and VeriSpecGen, with a human-reviewed and proven reference test set.
5IgalfMBKx.claimed_gains: SpecGen pass@4 on AuXSpec-Test improves 0.7% → 82.7% and 14.3% → 84.3% for the two models, the 27B model outperforms all frontier models, and both improve on Verina (including 7.0% → 90.5%, rest cut off); the TLDR instead gives 0.7% → 60.3% in-domain.
5IgalfMBKx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating a declarative postcondition from an executable checker is a useful way to get scalable feedback, with substantial dataset construction and validation, and that gains transfer to Verina.
5IgalfMBKx.main_concern: Reviewers say the closest baseline VeriSpecGen is not backbone-matched, the contribution of executable feedback is not isolated from the multi-part RL recipe, and accepted outputs can still be wrong (five false positives in 60 audited).

X3zSt6ILPn.one_liner: Represents a partner in the ego agent's own embedding space by applying a perspective transform to the ego's representation mechanism
X3zSt6ILPn.problem: It is unclear whether the human Like-Me inference principle, understanding others through one's own experience, gives a computational mechanism for partner modelling in multi-agent RL, especially with unseen partners.
X3zSt6ILPn.method: LIMI combines an estimate of the partner's perspective with the ego agent's own representation mechanism, in two variants: a fixed perspective transform needing no behavioural-prediction objective, and a learnt transform that learns the self-other mapping from partner behaviour. The authors also show theoretically that the benefit of adapting to a partner is bounded by how much partner information the hidden state encodes.
X3zSt6ILPn.key_idea: Encode the partner by passing an estimate of its perspective through the ego agent's own encoder, so self and other share one embedding space.
X3zSt6ILPn.evidence: Overcooked, multi-robot coordination, and embodied locomotion tasks, with probing of frozen representations and representational similarity analysis.
X3zSt6ILPn.claimed_gains: LIMI improves ad hoc teamwork in several settings, particularly when coordinating with unseen partners is difficult, and increases information about partners' actions and internal states; no numbers stated.
X3zSt6ILPn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the LIMI architecture is intuitive, simple, and well motivated, with clear exposition and analyses showing the benefit of ego representations as an inductive bias.
X3zSt6ILPn.main_concern: Reviewers say the environments are simple with heavily overlapping observations and shared action spaces, closely related ego-model work is not contrasted, and evidence for broader zero-shot coordination or for isolating the partner representation's effect is limited.

UqU6DTKKdH.one_liner: Selects on-policy distillation positions by unsigned future teacher-student mismatch and mixes signed future feedback into shaped directional coefficients.
UqU6DTKKdH.problem: On-policy distillation allocates dense token-level supervision using only local teacher-student disagreement, ignoring whether a disagreement persists or dissipates over the following trajectory.
UqU6DTKKdH.method: Advantage Credit Transfer (ACT) uses unsigned future mismatch over a short window to pick a sparse set of positions, then mixes signed future feedback into the shaped directional coefficients at those positions and leaves all others unchanged. It reuses teacher and student log probabilities already computed by OPD.
UqU6DTKKdH.key_idea: Decouples where to intervene (unsigned future mismatch, preserving disagreement before sign cancellation) from what correction to apply (signed future feedback that retains direction and net effect).
UqU6DTKKdH.evidence: Controlled experiments compare selectors at equal coverage, signed versus unsigned feedback under a fixed gate, and selective versus uniform allocation; reviews cite results on AIME 2024 and a multi-domain distillation setting (Tables 1-2).
UqU6DTKKdH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using future context beyond local disagreement is a reasonable direction and that ACT is cheap, needing no extra teacher queries, rollouts, or value network.
UqU6DTKKdH.main_concern: Gains over baselines in Table 1 are marginal (except AIME 2024) with no standard deviations or multi-seed runs, and the need for future information is not directly demonstrated.

NuVpQ65fHJ.one_liner: STAR converts psychological questionnaires into advice-seeking scenarios to compare LLM and human behavioral dispositions across 25 models.
NuVpQ65fHJ.problem: People increasingly seek social advice from LLMs, but self-reports may not transfer to actual advisory behavior, so alignment of LLM dispositions with human ones needs behavior-based measurement.
NuVpQ65fHJ.method: STAR adapts items from established psychological questionnaires into realistic advice-seeking situational judgment tests, yielding a dataset of 23k scenarios each validated by 3 raters and annotated with preferences from 10 participants. It then compares the choices of 25 LLMs with human choices.
NuVpQ65fHJ.key_idea: Converts self-descriptive questionnaire items into situational judgment scenarios with human-annotated preferences, so LLM recommendations can be compared against human consensus and diversity.
NuVpQ65fHJ.evidence: Evaluation of 25 LLMs on the 23k-scenario dataset, comparing model choices with human consensus, human disagreement, and the models' own self-reported values.
NuVpQ65fHJ.claimed_gains: Frontier models fail to reflect high human consensus in 15-20% of cases and smaller models fail at higher rates; benchmark findings, no method gains reported.
NuVpQ65fHJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the rigorous, human-validated dataset construction and the reuse of psychometric instruments converted into situational judgments.
NuVpQ65fHJ.main_concern: The premise that LLM consensus should mirror human consensus is questionable, and LLM-generated scenarios and the forced binary-choice format may introduce confounds and overstate the distributional-gap claims.

i1SbXixzzz.one_liner: Cross-Ego Contrastive Learning aligns synchronized teammate first-person views so one player's representation encodes teammates and opponents.
i1SbXixzzz.problem: In fast, reactive settings with limited communication, a team member must infer teammate locations and actions from its own first-person view, and it is unclear whether such allocentric awareness can be learned from coordinated team data.
i1SbXixzzz.method: The authors build X-Ego-CS, 273 hours of synchronized first-person gameplay from 101 high-skill Counter-Strike 2 matches with a 33-task benchmark, and train encoders with CECL, which aligns the representations of teammates' synchronized views.
i1SbXixzzz.key_idea: Contrastively aligns representations of simultaneous teammate views of the same match moment, pulling one agent's embedding toward team-state information at some cost to self-centric information.
i1SbXixzzz.evidence: Controlled experiments on held-out matches compare synchronized teammates against single-view adaptation and side- and phase-matched pseudo-teams, across encoders and prediction horizons, with shortcut checks; benchmark of 33 tasks.
i1SbXixzzz.claimed_gains: Qualitative only: other players' locations become more predictable across encoders and horizons at a cost to self-centric prediction; no gain figures stated in the abstract.
i1SbXixzzz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the dataset and benchmark and find the teammate-alignment contrastive objective simple and intuitive, with controls for shortcuts such as team side, game phase, bomb plants, and deaths.
i1SbXixzzz.main_concern: The paper does not show that better perception yields better gameplay or coordination, and pseudo-teams matched only on side and phase already recover about 70% of the gain, with small absolute gains.

Gn9bbQAwQD.one_liner: Two-stage sparse autoencoder whose Level-1 active features route to small residual-expert SAEs that encode the reconstruction residual.
Gn9bbQAwQD.problem: Scaling full-dictionary sparse autoencoders to capture diverse features in large language models is computationally expensive.
Gn9bbQAwQD.method: A lightweight Level-1 SAE forms an initial reconstruction and uses its active features to select residual experts, small Level-2 SAEs that encode the residual. A joint TopK allocates the Level-2 sparsity budget across the selected experts.
Gn9bbQAwQD.key_idea: Reuse the Level-1 SAE's active features as the router that picks small Level-2 residual experts, with a joint TopK splitting the sparsity budget across them.
Gn9bbQAwQD.evidence: Gemma-2-2B residual stream activations, compared with efficient SAE baselines at matched effective dictionary widths, sparsity, and encoder FLOPs, with ablations and auto-interpretability checks.
Gn9bbQAwQD.claimed_gains: Compared with 16K-feature full-dictionary baselines, ResSAE accesses a 135K-feature space with 56-74% fewer encoder FLOPs while achieving up to 11% lower reconstruction MSE.
Gn9bbQAwQD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple and sensible, combining residual reconstruction with feature-based routing, and report lower reconstruction error at matched encoder FLOPs.
Gn9bbQAwQD.main_concern: Encoder-FLOP savings translate into little training-time speedup (8.4 vs 9.0 hours), and the gain over SwitchSAEs is small and confounded by unequal tuning and token budgets.

aTR4IGyJOr.one_liner: Dataset guaranteeing single-modality answerability to measure modality distraction in VLMs, plus a weight-space robustness vector that reduces it.
aTR4IGyJOr.problem: VLMs can be distracted by irrelevant context from one modality even when it carries no useful information, and existing probes rarely establish single-modality answerability to isolate this failure.
aTR4IGyJOr.method: MoGround spans four visual domains with every answer available from exactly one modality, so distraction is measured as correct answers that flip to wrong ones once irrelevant content from the other modality is added. A weight-space robustness vector trained on one MoGround split mitigates it without extra inference passes.
aTR4IGyJOr.key_idea: Build questions answerable from exactly one modality so correct-to-wrong flips isolate distraction, then train a weight-space robustness vector on that signal to reduce it.
aTR4IGyJOr.evidence: Seven open-source VLMs on the four-domain dataset, with correlations between grounding strength and distraction, and held-out evaluation of the mitigation plus standard multimodal tasks.
aTR4IGyJOr.claimed_gains: The robustness vector reduces distraction on all seven models by 29% to 51% at a cost of only 0.1 average points of accuracy on standard multimodal tasks; the weaker-grounded modality is more distracted (r = +0.86) and distraction scales inversely with grounding strength (r = -0.90).
aTR4IGyJOr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark a clear, controlled, verified way to measure modality distraction, with extensive empirical analysis and a practical mitigation that adds no inference cost.
aTR4IGyJOr.main_concern: Novelty over prior modality-distraction work is limited, and a bag-of-words classifier predicts the grounding modality from question text at 95.7% accuracy, raising doubts that the vector learns more than surface cues.

qskQEF5nGW.one_liner: Paired-control evaluation requires matched brain input to beat both zeroed and shuffled controls on NLL for brain-conditioned language models.
qskQEF5nGW.problem: Continuous side signals can change a language model's output distribution without improving prediction, so distribution deformation alone does not show brain conditioning is useful.
qskQEF5nGW.method: Matched brain input must improve prediction over removal (ZERO) and mismatch (SHUF) controls, quantified with Jensen-Shannon divergence and next-token NLL. It is tested in synthetic TVB experiments and on real MEG-MASC with a T5 cross-attention model over post-word MEG windows.
qskQEF5nGW.key_idea: Require matched brain input to outperform both a removal control (ZERO) and a mismatch control (SHUF), separating useful deformation from generic perturbation.
qskQEF5nGW.evidence: Synthetic TVB experiments and MEG-MASC with random, story-blocked, subject-blocked, and leave-one-subject-out splits, plus mismatch-control variants, Gaussian null streams, a BERT positive control, and an fMRI reanalysis per reviews.
qskQEF5nGW.claimed_gains: Matched MEG improves target-word NLL over both zeroed and shuffled MEG on random, story-blocked, and subject-blocked splits, with DeltaNLL gains of roughly 0.08-0.11.
qskQEF5nGW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper shows a mismatch control alone gives an incomplete evaluation, and credit the careful MEG experiments with varied mismatch controls, Gaussian nulls, and a positive control.
qskQEF5nGW.main_concern: Missing baselines and limited novelty: ZERO uses the adapted model rather than an off-the-shelf or neural-free matched model, the absolute gain over a non-neural baseline is unclear, and two-control permutation logic is already standard in multimodal analysis.

puc8b9cUyy.one_liner: World action model built from event-level video pretraining, single-step distillation into a visual planner, and a mixture-of-transformers action module.
puc8b9cUyy.problem: Existing world action models often predict incorrect motion in open-ended environments because base video models are not tuned for manipulation and adding action components degrades video generalization.
puc8b9cUyy.method: VPP2 continues pretraining a video foundation model on a curated large-scale manipulation video dataset with detailed captions and event-level clips, then post-trains and distills it into a single-step fixed-horizon visual planner. An action module via a mixture-of-transformers learns an implicit inverse dynamics model.
puc8b9cUyy.key_idea: Pretrain the video model on complete manipulation events with detailed captions, distill to a single-step planner, and decode actions via MoT implicit inverse dynamics.
puc8b9cUyy.evidence: Video-prediction instruction-following comparison against Cosmos3-64B, plus zero-shot manipulation evaluations on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-OOD, RoboDojo, and ALOHA per the reviews.
puc8b9cUyy.claimed_gains: VPP2-14B outperforms Cosmos3-64B by 11% in instruction following on open-ended video prediction; the remaining results are cut off in the abstract.
puc8b9cUyy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree on strong empirical results (LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-OOD, RoboDojo), a clear event-level data curation and captioning pipeline, and a useful staged training recipe.
puc8b9cUyy.main_concern: The benefit of event-level pretraining for downstream policy performance is not isolated from captioning and data effects, and one reviewer finds the work unreproducible with unclear research insight.

4GHQGXqnsa.one_liner: Monocular 4D reconstruction with ray-constrained 3D track queries tied to shared SE(3) motion nodes under a continuous-time prior.
4GHQGXqnsa.problem: Long-range tracks give geometric constraints for dynamic monocular scenes, but their fragmented temporal coverage is hard to integrate into shared, continuous motion.
4GHQGXqnsa.method: Each track gets a reference-time 3D query constrained to its camera ray, and image and depth observations constrain shared latent motion nodes holding an SE(3) pose and body-frame velocity at sparse support times. A white-noise-on-acceleration prior couples neighboring nodes and gives continuous-time interpolation, and motion transfers to Gaussians by dual-quaternion blending with local SE(3) residuals for non-rigid deformation.
4GHQGXqnsa.key_idea: Separate track measurements from latent 3D motion states, so tracks visible at different times jointly constrain the same smooth SE(3) motion nodes.
4GHQGXqnsa.evidence: Diverse monocular dynamic scenes on two benchmarks, with component ablations (abstract is truncated).
4GHQGXqnsa.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that it achieves competitive novel-view synthesis quality and improves structural and temporal consistency under rapid motion, with the rest truncated.
4GHQGXqnsa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating measurements from motion states is a coherent design grounded in continuous-time state estimation, with consistent results and informative ablations.
4GHQGXqnsa.main_concern: Claimed robustness to rapid motion and incomplete tracks lacks controlled tests such as dropping tracks or stratifying by speed, and novelty is incremental relative to MoSca-style multi-node blending.

24M9WCQ3yc.one_liner: Generates clarification tasks by planting defects in certified statecharts rendered as PRDs, scoring agents on defect detection and restraint.
24M9WCQ3yc.problem: Measuring whether coding agents notice incomplete or inconsistent specifications, and avoid inventing problems in complete ones, needs ground truth that is not a matter of judgment.
24M9WCQ3yc.method: PM Bench starts from a certified statechart, plants controlled defects (an unreachable state, conflicting transitions, a counter overflow), and renders a Product Requirements Document. A hidden LLM judge maps agent claims to planted defects and lists unsupported claims, which code checks against formal oracle facts.
24M9WCQ3yc.key_idea: Use a formalism (statecharts) as the source of truth for task generation, answer key, and grading, with detection and restraint as paired scores.
24M9WCQ3yc.evidence: Eleven models evaluated with review instructions that name no defect kinds, plus a prose-style experiment on four models (per reviews).
24M9WCQ3yc.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract only says that Fable 5 leads among the eleven models evaluated.
24M9WCQ3yc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalism-based construction gives verifiable ground truth and that including defect-free specifications to measure restraint is useful.
24M9WCQ3yc.main_concern: The benchmark relies on template-generated statecharts unlike real requirements, and grading still uses an LLM judge whose reliability and judge-dependence are untested.

0IoaApelMX.one_liner: Training-free masked-diffusion LLM sampler scoring token compatibility by effective resistance on attention graphs to capture multi-hop dependencies.
0IoaApelMX.problem: Attention-based dependency-aware samplers for parallel decoding use only direct (single-hop) attention edges, missing indirect dependencies and so can unmask incompatible tokens together.
0IoaApelMX.method: GRID replaces the direct-edge coupling score with effective resistance on the graph of masked positions, which aggregates direct and indirect routes between positions. The paper also introduces Dep-Bench, a controlled benchmark with five datasets spanning four graph structures.
0IoaApelMX.key_idea: Score coupling between masked positions by the effective resistance of the attention-derived graph, a parameter-free measure aggregating direct and indirect paths, instead of raw attention weights.
0IoaApelMX.evidence: Dep-Bench with known dependencies at varying depths, ParallelBench, and 16 combinations of leading models and LLM reasoning benchmarks.
0IoaApelMX.claimed_gains: Up to x2 decoding-step speedup over the fastest competing sampler on ParallelBench at 95% of top-1 quality, and 3-10x speedup over top-1 decoding across 16 model-benchmark combinations (TL;DR: 7-11% over the fastest competing sampler).
0IoaApelMX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-hop dependency idea well motivated and supported by controlled dependency tests and evaluation across several models and benchmarks.
0IoaApelMX.main_concern: Gains are confounded by additional tuned components (GRID is tuned on HumanEval and evaluated on it), so effective resistance's independent contribution is unclear, and novelty over DAWN is questioned.

QcOwunDUt0.one_liner: Fully dynamic algorithm for monotone submodular maximization under a matroid using deletion-tolerant exchange certificates and hierarchical rebuilding.
QcOwunDUt0.problem: Fully dynamic monotone submodular maximization under a matroid constraint of rank at most k lacked an algorithm with polylogarithmic update time and no polynomial dependence on k.
QcOwunDUt0.method: A randomized algorithm maintains a feasible set under oblivious insertions and deletions using a deletion-tolerant exchange certificate that charges the optimum to frozen weights of retained and deleted acceptances, combined with deterministic hierarchical rebuilding. Exact truncated sampling controls expected deletion loss and leaves small residuals for later rebuilding levels.
QcOwunDUt0.key_idea: Charge the optimum to frozen weights of retained and deleted acceptances, and push small residuals from truncated sampling to later hierarchical rebuilding levels.
QcOwunDUt0.evidence: Theoretical analysis against oblivious update sequences; no experiments stated.
QcOwunDUt0.claimed_gains: Expected value at least (1/4 - epsilon) times OPT at every fixed time, with total oracle queries O((n/epsilon) log^3(k/epsilon) log(2k) log^2(2n)), i.e. polylogarithmic amortized queries for fixed epsilon.
QcOwunDUt0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is an important theoretical result that removes polynomial dependence on the matroid rank with polylogarithmic amortized query cost.
QcOwunDUt0.main_concern: The bound is amortized and not uniformly better than Banihashem et al. (2024), which has a per-update guarantee and a smaller epsilon and log n dependence, and there is no empirical evaluation.

vwnMXQxYsb.one_liner: GroupRoute routes queries to task groups using early-layer instruction embeddings of a frozen LM, reducing forgetting in continual instruction tuning.
vwnMXQxYsb.problem: Without task identifiers at inference, whole-prompt representations entangle the requested operation with input content, confusing tasks with similar inputs.
vwnMXQxYsb.method: Instruction representations from layers 1-3 of a frozen LM identify tasks. GroupRoute groups related tasks as they arrive, guides training within each group, and routes queries to groups with no trainable routing parameters; InK learns all tasks in one adapter.
vwnMXQxYsb.key_idea: Route and group tasks from instruction-only embeddings taken at the earliest transformer layers of a frozen backbone, with unmatched queries sent to the frozen model.
vwnMXQxYsb.evidence: Experiments on three backbone models and three benchmarks (SuperNatural Instructions, TRACE, ProgressivePrompts), with ablations over InfLoRA, O-LoRA and DualPrompt.
vwnMXQxYsb.claimed_gains: Instruction-only routing reaches 99.4-99.7% task identification accuracy on a shared-corpus benchmark even with reworded instructions; other numbers not stated in the abstract excerpt.
vwnMXQxYsb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating the instruction from input content is practical, the router needs no training, and GroupRoute improves several underlying continual learning methods.
vwnMXQxYsb.main_concern: The default grouping yields nearly one group per task (35 groups for 42 tasks), so gains may come from parameter isolation rather than the grouping insight.

6UekdpgCft.one_liner: Continual learning for EEG foundation models using a Time-Space-Frequency basis from physiological descriptors to constrain feature drift without replay.
6UekdpgCft.problem: Protected parameters lose importance as the shared EEG model evolves, and fixed replay buffers cover a shrinking share of heterogeneous historical EEG knowledge.
6UekdpgCft.method: Constructs a Time-Space-Frequency (TSF) basis from current-task descriptors and frozen previous-model features, transfers the teacher's relations among examples, and preserves TSF coupling during adaptation, with accumulated TSF-related directions constraining feature drift.
6UekdpgCft.key_idea: Anchor continual adaptation to a TSF basis of physiological descriptors that stays meaningful as parameters change, constraining drift along accumulated TSF directions instead of replaying data.
6UekdpgCft.evidence: Task-incremental experiments on nine datasets, six paradigms, and four EEG foundation models against 18 continual learning baselines, with ablations.
6UekdpgCft.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest average anytime accuracy and backward transfer and the lowest forgetting among 18 methods in task-incremental experiments; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
6UekdpgCft.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important, the method clearly motivated with interpretable TSF control, and the evaluation broad across nine datasets, four foundation models, and 18 baselines, with careful ablations.
6UekdpgCft.main_concern: Reproducibility and fairness gaps: replay buffer budgets and data splits are not specified, the storage cost of the frozen backbone is not accounted for, and the discriminative value of TSF subspaces is insufficiently justified.

iqIuIKzPTq.one_liner: Fully first-order double-loop algorithm for contextual stochastic bilevel optimization, accelerated with random truncated multilevel Monte Carlo.
iqIuIKzPTq.problem: Contextual stochastic bilevel optimization is computationally hard because of its semi-infinite nature, and many algorithms for stochastic bilevel optimization do not apply.
iqIuIKzPTq.method: A double-loop algorithm uses only first-order derivatives of the lower-level objective g. An accelerated version adds random truncated multilevel Monte Carlo (RT-MLMC) and an adaptive stepsize for empirical stabilization.
iqIuIKzPTq.key_idea: Replace Hessian-based hypergradients with a penalty-based first-order estimator, and cut inner-loop cost with random truncated multilevel Monte Carlo.
iqIuIKzPTq.evidence: Complexity proofs plus numerical experiments on meta-learning and a contextual electricity pricing problem against existing methods.
iqIuIKzPTq.claimed_gains: Expected sample and gradient complexity of O~(eps^-6) for the basic algorithm and O~(eps^-4) for the accelerated one, matching Hessian-based CSBO algorithms.
iqIuIKzPTq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the first fully first-order method for CSBO with general context distributions, with sound analysis and rates matching known Hessian-based results.
iqIuIKzPTq.main_concern: Practical value is unclear: the contribution looks incremental over existing techniques, the faster-rate algorithm converges slower in one experiment, and only two applications are tested.

03ELNqpOT7.one_liner: Feature-recovery metric showing unlearned models can match retrained outputs while encoding different features, with supporting theory.
03ELNqpOT7.problem: Standard post-deletion metrics compare outputs only, concealing differences in the features an unlearned model and a retrained model encode.
03ELNqpOT7.method: The paper proves that models agreeing on outputs but encoding different features can disagree after one gradient step on their prediction heads, and that deleting a small data fraction can make retraining select different features. It introduces a feature-recovery measure that separates missing from extraneous features and applies it to eight unlearning methods.
03ELNqpOT7.key_idea: Compare the features encoded by unlearned versus retrained models, separating retrained features the unlearned model lacks from extra features it keeps, instead of comparing outputs.
03ELNqpOT7.evidence: Theory (an XOR construction per reviewers) plus experiments on eight unlearning methods, mainly CIFAR-100 and SVHN, with relearning and downstream-adaptation tests.
03ELNqpOT7.reviewer_consensus: Distinguishing forgetting information from recovering the features retraining would learn is a fresh, cleanly proved framing, with experiments that go beyond standard unlearning evaluations.
03ELNqpOT7.main_concern: The feature metric rests on one operationalization (PCA-response clustering following Jiang et al.) that is sensitive to several hyperparameters, with limited datasets and novelty overlapping prior work on residual knowledge.

kz4LsXfdX1.one_liner: Detects memorized prompts in text-to-image diffusion models using the conditional score's Jacobian at the prompt embedding.
kz4LsXfdX1.problem: The conditional-minus-unconditional score difference used to detect memorization does not reveal where along the prompt-embedding path the conditional score changes.
kz4LsXfdX1.method: The score difference is written as the norm of the integral of the conditional score's derivative along a linear interpolation from the unconditional to the prompt embedding. Memorized prompts show a sharp rise near the prompt embedding, which is measured with the condition Jacobian evaluated at the prompt embedding.
kz4LsXfdX1.key_idea: Memorized prompts show a sharp change of the conditional score near the prompt embedding, captured by the Jacobian of the score with respect to the condition.
kz4LsXfdX1.evidence: Detection experiments across architectures, noise samples, and reduced latent resolutions; per reviews, a two-feature variant uses a logistic-regression decision boundary.
kz4LsXfdX1.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract gives no numeric detection results.
kz4LsXfdX1.reviewer_consensus: The line-integral view of the score difference is new and insightful, the paper is clear, and the detector improves AUC and TPR at low false-positive rates over prior work across architectures.
kz4LsXfdX1.main_concern: The benchmark is near saturated and may confound memorization with prompt-source differences, the logistic-regression fusion needs memorized examples, and runtime and memory costs are not reported.

9ZVvqVYAF6.one_liner: Proves ambient ReLU score-network diffusion models attain intrinsic-dimension Wasserstein rates on smooth manifolds, with explicit polynomial dependence on ambient dimension.
9ZVvqVYAF6.problem: Diffusion models learn scores in ambient space, and earlier 1-Wasserstein bounds for ambient score-network ERM leave the dependence on the ambient dimension D untracked.
9ZVvqVYAF6.method: A constructive analysis of empirical risk minimization over ambient score networks for beta-Holder densities on compact d-dimensional manifolds in R^D, using a finite-anchor Gauss-Newton network that approximates the nearest-point projection, tangent-cell approximations at moderate and high noise, and a low-noise score expansion centered at the projection.
9ZVvqVYAF6.key_idea: Approximate the nearest-point projection onto the manifold with a finite-anchor Gauss-Newton network and center the low-noise score expansion on it.
9ZVvqVYAF6.evidence: Theory only: a bound on the expected 1-Wasserstein error of the cube-projected continuous-time sampler; the abstract also mentions a matching lower bound (text cut off).
9ZVvqVYAF6.claimed_gains: For d>2, expected 1-Wasserstein error is at most D^p n^{-(beta+1)/(2beta+d)} up to logarithmic factors, with explicit exponent p = max{ceil(6 beta)+8, ceil(5d/4)+13}.
9ZVvqVYAF6.reviewer_consensus: An end-to-end analysis that includes sampler error with explicit rates, plus an original low-noise treatment centered at the nearest-point projection and a sound proof strategy.
9ZVvqVYAF6.main_concern: The contribution relative to Tang & Yang (2024) and later work is unclear since prior rates reach the same intrinsic exponent, and the D^{O(d)} factor is large compared with other recent bounds.

aCaaVRzpI5.one_liner: Multi-view robot world model using calibrated image-space action conditions, counterfactual post-training, and an embodied video reward model for RL.
aCaaVRzpI5.problem: Imprecise calibration impairs action following in robot video prediction, and limited coverage of unsuccessful interactions biases predictions toward successful outcomes.
aCaaVRzpI5.method: Action trajectories are rendered into image-space conditions aligned to videos via offline geometric calibration, and the model is post-trained on counterfactual edited action trajectories. A video reward model trained on a human-annotated robot, object, and interaction defect dataset scores predictions to guide reinforcement-learning post-training.
aCaaVRzpI5.key_idea: Generate futures from edited counterfactual actions and optimize them with RL against a reward model trained on human-annotated robot, object, and interaction defects.
aCaaVRzpI5.evidence: AgiBot evaluations with human assessment, calibration ablations, a RoboTwin policy-evaluation study, and the AgiBot World Challenge 2026 world model track.
aCaaVRzpI5.claimed_gains: On AgiBot it reduces the human-assessed interaction defect rate from 48.12% to 6.25% and ranks first in the world model track of the AgiBot World Challenge 2026.
aCaaVRzpI5.reviewer_consensus: Offline geometric calibration and a unified image-space action representation are practical, with ablations showing improved alignment and action following and human evaluation supporting the post-training gains.
aCaaVRzpI5.main_concern: Stage II bundles counterfactual actions, reward supervision, and RL, so ablations do not isolate counterfactual data from reward optimization, and the reward model never sees the action condition.

950or2jh05.one_liner: Learns sparse nonnegative skill coordinates for tasks and agents from success records and frozen task embeddings, predicting log-odds of success.
950or2jh05.problem: Agents are summarized either by aggregate benchmark scores that say nothing about individual tasks or by latent embeddings whose coordinates carry no fixed meaning.
950or2jh05.method: Each task places sparse nonnegative demands on shared coordinates and each agent has abilities on them, with predicted log-odds of success equal to global ability plus a demand-weighted ability-difficulty gap per demanded skill. Training uses binary success records and frozen task embeddings, with no skill taxonomy, annotations, or task metadata.
950or2jh05.key_idea: Factor item-level success into task demands and agent abilities on 8 to 32 shared sparse coordinates inside an item-response-theory log-odds model.
950or2jh05.evidence: Comparison with dense amortized item response theory on EmbedLLM and RouterBench, plus a controlled pool of 16 agents with withheld profiles (text cut off).
950or2jh05.claimed_gains: Passing predictions through 8 to 32 shared coordinates costs at most 0.3 percentage points against dense amortized item response theory on EmbedLLM and RouterBench.
950or2jh05.reviewer_consensus: Interpretable skill coordinates are an appealing alternative to aggregate scores and opaque embeddings, with a simple method and experiments across a broad range of settings.
950or2jh05.main_concern: The learned basis depends on the training seed and lacks a clear, unique interpretation, and there is no comparison against other ways of inferring skills or learning joint task-agent embeddings.

g9IbGtyrtP.one_liner: On-policy distillation where a fixed teacher picks one of several student-proposed responses before execution, shaping the states future training uses.
g9IbGtyrtP.problem: In multi-turn on-policy distillation, student action errors alter the environment and undermine the conditions for effective teacher supervision at later turns.
g9IbGtyrtP.method: At each turn the student proposes several candidate responses and a fixed teacher selects one for execution before it reaches the environment. Only the selected response is kept for distillation and appended to the interaction history with the resulting observation.
g9IbGtyrtP.key_idea: Let the teacher choose among student candidates before execution, so guidance shapes both the supervised response and subsequent interaction states while the student remains the only response source.
g9IbGtyrtP.evidence: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop across multiple model scales and initialization settings, with ablations against random and student selection.
g9IbGtyrtP.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says student task performance improves across scales and initializations without giving numbers.
g9IbGtyrtP.reviewer_consensus: A simple, clearly presented idea whose ablations attribute gains to teacher selection rather than random or student selection, with consistent improvement over vanilla on-policy distillation.
g9IbGtyrtP.main_concern: Main comparisons match update counts although the method costs about 1.2 to 2.2 times the training time of vanilla distillation, and related methods (Guided-OPD, SAGE-OPD) and SFT or RL student baselines are not evaluated.

JBSJpyvmCe.one_liner: Training-free Mamba-2 prefill speedup that restricts recurrence length in heads with short effective recurrence and corrects chunk-boundary contributions.
JBSJpyvmCe.problem: Mamba-2's SSD accounts for under 5% of FLOPs yet nearly 20% of prefill latency because it applies full recurrence uniformly although heads differ in temporal range.
JBSJpyvmCe.method: SERESA defines Effective Recurrence Length (ERL), sets the number of restricted heads from its distribution, and selects heads retaining the most contribution within a prescribed recurrence length. It reduces their intra- and inter-chunk computation and recovers boundary-crossing contributions through boundary correction, leaving full recurrence for the remaining heads.
JBSJpyvmCe.key_idea: Keep full recurrence only for the few heads with long effective recurrence and truncate it for the rest, selected by coverage within a fixed length.
JBSJpyvmCe.evidence: ERL analysis across models showing stable head ordering across input distributions, kernel timing, perplexity, and a downstream comparison per reviews.
JBSJpyvmCe.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract gives only the motivating figures that SSD is under 5% of FLOPs but nearly 20% of prefill latency.
JBSJpyvmCe.reviewer_consensus: A clear, simple, training-free insight that long-range recurrence is concentrated in a minority of heads, with ablations showing coverage-based head selection beats decay-only or learned-gate selection.
JBSJpyvmCe.main_concern: The end-to-end gain is modest (about 1.1x on its own), quality evidence beyond perplexity is limited, and comparison with prior local-versus-global head work such as LongMamba is missing.

NyCt5aiavN.one_liner: Shows verifier filtering before LLM fusion lowers accuracy because fusers correct errors using incorrect candidates.
NyCt5aiavN.problem: Pipelines such as Archon place a verifier before a fuser on the assumption that discarding incorrect candidates can only help synthesis.
NyCt5aiavN.method: An empirical study on MATH-500 compares five 8B process-reward-model-filtered pipelines against unfiltered critique-and-fuse, with a 2x2 factorial separating critiques from candidate retention and a three-tier accuracy decomposition that predicts the false-positive and false-negative asymmetry.
NyCt5aiavN.key_idea: Generator outputs are polarized, so a verifier acts only on a thin mixed tier while the fuser corrects errors using incorrect candidates as signal; critiques, not retention, prevent corruption.
NyCt5aiavN.evidence: MATH-500 only, with five 8B process reward models and a controlled 2x2 factorial.
NyCt5aiavN.claimed_gains: Verifier-filtered pipelines reach 0.712-0.778 accuracy versus 0.930 for unfiltered critique-and-fuse (a loss of 15.2-21.8 points), and the fuser rescues 61.6% of all-wrong problems, raising the generator ceiling from 0.828 to 0.930.
NyCt5aiavN.reviewer_consensus: A counterintuitive and useful finding that challenges the select-then-synthesize default, backed by a clear analysis that isolates a mechanism.
NyCt5aiavN.main_concern: The headline comparison confounds filtering with critiques (critique-and-fuse gets critiques, the gated pipeline does not), and the evidence is limited to the single MATH-500 benchmark.

VTsuAUDmeN.one_liner: Agent memory framework that offloads inactive KV states to CPU and restores selected turns with updated positions, without re-prefilling text.
VTsuAUDmeN.problem: Summarizing agent histories can discard details needed later, while recalling historical text repeats prefill computation.
VTsuAUDmeN.method: RETURN keeps active context compact while retaining historical KV states; an ephemeral probe selects history from turn digests and then rolls back its tokens and execution state so memory management stays outside the task trace. Path-aware parallel replay reconstructs recorded selections and position mappings and propagates gradients through reused states.
VTsuAUDmeN.key_idea: Restore selected historical KV with remapped positions and run history selection as a rolled-back ephemeral probe, so memory management leaves no trace in the task context.
VTsuAUDmeN.evidence: Memory and agentic benchmarks (six benchmarks and three models per reviews), serving throughput measurements, and on-policy distillation with parallel replay.
VTsuAUDmeN.reviewer_consensus: Separating memory management from task generation via ephemeral probe rollback enables training-free use and full-context teacher supervision, with evaluation across multiple benchmarks and models showing active-context savings.
VTsuAUDmeN.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed: all backbones are hybrid models whose recurrent layers still see the full history, KV-selection baselines such as InfLLM and QUEST are missing, and serving gains come mainly from CPU offloading.

WdMtlG7LnC.one_liner: Training-dynamics analysis of a two-block Transformer showing causal masking drives first-token attention sinks and frequent tokens absorb attention.
WdMtlG7LnC.problem: The theoretical origin of attention sinks, and how they emerge spontaneously during training, is insufficiently understood.
WdMtlG7LnC.method: The paper theoretically analyzes a two-block Transformer trained on synthetic text datasets, showing that causal masking makes first-token parameters accumulate disproportionate gradients while high-frequency semantic tokens receive larger gradients and absorb attention. It also shows sinks remain compatible with predictive capacity.
WdMtlG7LnC.key_idea: Causal masking concentrates gradient on first-token parameters and high-frequency tokens receive larger gradients, so attention collapses onto them during training.
WdMtlG7LnC.evidence: Theoretical gradient analysis of a two-block Transformer on synthetic text data, with numerical experiments (reviewers note one main-text figure and single runs).
WdMtlG7LnC.reviewer_consensus: The question is well posed and the analysis is in-depth and rigorous for the simplified setting, offering a plausible explanation of attention sinks.
WdMtlG7LnC.main_concern: Scope and novelty are limited: a toy two-block setting, few experiments testing concrete predictions, little implication for deeper real networks, and earlier training-dynamics work on attention sinks.

sM7QnwZFfP.one_liner: Image-editing framework that adapts reasoning depth to instruction complexity via structured lens planning, trained jointly with GRPO and Flow-GRPO.
sM7QnwZFfP.problem: SFT-based reasoning for image editing applies the same deliberation depth to trivial and complex edits, and longer reasoning does not improve edits (GPT-Score about 5.2 even when the reasoning budget is tripled).
sM7QnwZFfP.method: PRISM decomposes pre-generation deliberation into three stages (complexity steering, tailored lens generation, ordered lens execution) distilled into per-sample actions that drive a flow-matching generation expert. The understanding and generation experts are trained jointly via GRPO and Flow-GRPO.
sM7QnwZFfP.key_idea: Choose reasoning depth from predicted complexity and execute it as ordered structured lenses, combining adaptive length with structured templates rather than using either alone.
sM7QnwZFfP.evidence: A diagnostic study of BAGEL, then evaluation on KRIS, RISE, PICA, GEdit-R, and ImgEdit with ablations and a REVISE-50K training set (per reviews).
sM7QnwZFfP.claimed_gains: In the diagnostic study, structural directives at the same reasoning budget raise GPT-Score from about 5.2 to 6.1; the abstract text is cut off before PRISM's benchmark numbers.
sM7QnwZFfP.reviewer_consensus: The finding that more reasoning can hurt editing is interesting, supported by thorough diagnostics and clear gains on reasoning-heavy benchmarks such as KRIS and PICA.
sM7QnwZFfP.main_concern: Attribution is weak: there is no adaptive-but-unstructured baseline, BAGEL variants are not fine-tuned on the same data, and baseline scores are inconsistent between figures and tables.

aKSQNU4abG.one_liner: Controlled study of how parallel data, code mixing, and complementary information in multilingual pretraining data affect cross-lingual knowledge transfer.
aKSQNU4abG.problem: Factors governing cross-lingual knowledge transfer in multilingual LMs are poorly understood, and past studies disagree on what counts as transfer and which factors matter.
aKSQNU4abG.method: Language models are trained from scratch on a synthetic multilingual corpus of biographies while data composition is varied, and the findings are then checked by continually pre-training off-the-shelf models on new knowledge and on a two-hop question-answering task.
aKSQNU4abG.key_idea: Vary how parallel, code-mixed, and complementary data are composed in a synthetic biography corpus to isolate which patterns unlock cross-lingual fact recall.
aKSQNU4abG.evidence: A controlled synthetic biography setting, real-world continual pre-training of off-the-shelf models (Wikipedia documents per reviews), and a two-hop QA task.
aKSQNU4abG.reviewer_consensus: Controlled and real-world settings with a clear definition of cross-lingual transfer yield actionable data-curation recipes.
aKSQNU4abG.main_concern: Training token counts differ across data compositions (for example about 13M for the baseline versus 26M to 48M for others), confounding composition with data and compute amount.

4LoEI7SX1s.one_liner: Explorer and solver agents self-generate tasks; heuristics from solver failures enter a memory bank only after repeated validated success.
4LoEI7SX1s.problem: LLM agents lack operational knowledge of new environments and repeat mistakes, while existing memory relies on human-written guidelines or on training tasks with oracle verifiers.
4LoEI7SX1s.method: An explorer interacts with the environment to generate challenging yet solvable tasks and a solver attempts them. A heuristic is derived from each solver failure and accepted only after the solver repeatedly succeeds with it in context, outcomes feed back to tune task difficulty, and accepted heuristics are consolidated into a memory bank.
4LoEI7SX1s.key_idea: Accept a heuristic into memory only if placing it in context turns a solver failure into repeated successes, using self-generated tasks and no oracle rewards.
4LoEI7SX1s.evidence: AppWorld, tau2-bench, and AutomationBench against a no-memory baseline and methods that use training tasks.
4LoEI7SX1s.claimed_gains: Improves mean success rates by up to 13.2 percentage points and pass^5 by up to 1.8x over a no-memory baseline, and is competitive with methods using training tasks.
4LoEI7SX1s.reviewer_consensus: The task-generation loop with validated heuristic acceptance is interesting, with consistent improvements over no memory on all three benchmarks and well-designed ablations.
4LoEI7SX1s.main_concern: Uncertainty is underestimated and baselines are reimplemented: one memory bank per method, small test sets with some gains under 2 sigma, and more solver rollouts than most baselines.

3v4Wat9SHS.one_liner: Ontology-based intermediate representation separating agent harness semantic mechanisms from execution policies for cross-runtime transfer.
3v4Wat9SHS.problem: Agent harness knowledge is coupled to framework-specific control structures, making a tuned harness hard to reuse and verify across runtimes while preserving its behavior.
3v4Wat9SHS.method: A Harness ontology gives a shared semantic space for constructs from different runtimes, and HarnessIR splits a harness into semantic mechanisms (reusable objects and stable dependencies) and execution policies (how mechanisms are selected, composed, and constrained). It is evaluated on a new benchmark, HarnessIR-Bench.
3v4Wat9SHS.key_idea: Compile harnesses into a runtime-independent IR via a shared ontology, separating which mechanisms exist from the policies governing how they are used.
3v4Wat9SHS.evidence: HarnessIR-Bench with ten single-task workflows and several source runtimes and LLMs (DeepSeek and GLM per reviews), comparing semantic and behavioral preservation against baselines.
3v4Wat9SHS.reviewer_consensus: Cross-runtime harness transfer is a practical, well-motivated problem, and the compiler-style IR is intuitive and supported by a new benchmark.
3v4Wat9SHS.main_concern: The benchmark is small (ten workflows, one generation per target) with unclear behavioral scoring, no clear statistically significant end-to-end gain over baselines, and no direct check of recovered IR accuracy.
