dPVQubEmwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating EEG as coarse evidence for discrete motion primitives is a sensible design, clearly presented, with informative ablations and analyses.
dPVQubEmwg.main_concern: Evaluation fairness and robustness are questioned: baselines get less tuning and capacity than NeuroAction, between-subject variability is large (standard deviations comparable to means), and reconstruction from the full EEG segment does not match the stated online-control motivation.

LIgMvRMUdA.one_liner: Scaling law for mixed-precision quantized pretraining that models forward and backward quantization separately, including a persistent optimization error floor.
LIgMvRMUdA.problem: Existing quantization scaling laws do not accurately account for mixed precision across the forward and backward passes and across layers.
LIgMvRMUdA.method: Separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency and models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. Existing 4-bit recipes are first decomposed into forward and backward components to choose fitting regimes, and the law is extended to layer-wise mixed precision to find the optimal recipe under a hardware-aware compute budget.
LIgMvRMUdA.key_idea: Add a persistent forward/backward quantization error term, separate from capacity loss, to the loss scaling law, then solve for optimal per-layer precision under a compute budget.
LIgMvRMUdA.evidence: Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes plus published Llama-style experiments, with a decomposition of existing 4-bit recipes (reviewers cite a 375-run Qwen3 grid).
LIgMvRMUdA.claimed_gains: Predicts loss with up to 11x lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale, and predicts that optimal precision increases with the compute budget.
LIgMvRMUdA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating forward and backward quantization effects and adding an irreducible error floor is an interpretable improvement over prior scaling laws, supported by a controlled experimental grid.
LIgMvRMUdA.main_concern: Evidence for the persistent-error term and the compute-optimal conclusions is thin: extrapolations are short (about 1.4x in size and 1.2x in data), fitted parameters look over-parametrized, and absolute prediction improvements are small.

QTc2Zrx0zK.one_liner: Benchmark of 15 image watermarking methods with matched data, an attack-strength index, and a message-recovery metric (QSR).
QTc2Zrx0zK.problem: Existing watermark benchmarks compare in-generation and post-hoc methods on inconsistent data, use uneven attack settings, and use bit accuracy that does not show whether the decoded message retains its meaning.
QTc2Zrx0zK.method: SEALBench evaluates 4 in-generation and 11 post-hoc methods on 25,864 real, 15,000 manipulated, and 12,665 synthetic images under four attack categories. It proposes the attack-strength index (ASI), which scores each attacked image against its own unattacked image with an image-quality metric, and Question Success Rate (QSR), which tests whether a frozen language model can answer questions from the extracted text.
QTc2Zrx0zK.key_idea: Normalize attack strength by image-quality distance to the unattacked image, and judge message recovery by whether a frozen language model can answer questions from the decoded text.
QTc2Zrx0zK.evidence: Four attack categories, from single image transformations to editing or watermark removal followed by additional processing (52 attack conditions per a reviewer), over real, manipulated, and synthetic images.
QTc2Zrx0zK.claimed_gains: not stated (benchmark paper; the findings are cut off in the abstract).
QTc2Zrx0zK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating in-generation and post-hoc methods on the same images, prompts, seeds, and messages with calibrated thresholds makes cross-family comparison more meaningful, and that QSR adds a useful view beyond bit accuracy.
QTc2Zrx0zK.main_concern: Findings are largely descriptive, the 52 attack conditions are mostly parameter variants and compositions of few attacks, and ASI and QSR are not well validated (QSR depends on payload encoding without error correction).

6mskY8CVNA.one_liner: Casts audio description as a mixed-integer program jointly choosing what to describe, when to speak, and how to phrase it.
6mskY8CVNA.problem: Existing automatic audio description systems treat generation as local video-to-text with content and timing already given, whereas real AD needs coupled decisions about narrative importance, timing that avoids dialogue, and fit within the available time.
6mskY8CVNA.method: LLMs propose and ground visual elements, estimate their salience to the narrative, and generate compressed realizations. A mixed-integer linear program then jointly selects and schedules descriptions across a scene subject to temporal constraints.
6mskY8CVNA.key_idea: Let LLMs produce candidate descriptions with salience estimates and compressed variants, then select and place them with a MILP enforcing temporal gap and non-overlap constraints.
6mskY8CVNA.evidence: The REFRAMED benchmark for realistic audio description of movies, compared with prompted LLMs, with ablations on temporal constraints and salience estimation.
6mskY8CVNA.claimed_gains: Beats prompted LLMs on what to describe and when, with the best narrative QA and temporally grounded metrics reported; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
6mskY8CVNA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing content selection, timing, and compression is a meaningful, more realistic formulation, with an interpretable MILP and ablations that support it.
6mskY8CVNA.main_concern: The comparison with the LLM scheduler is not like-for-like (its prompt omits the MILP's constraints), narrative gains are small and uneven, and there is no human evaluation.

TYPdMlmbBX.one_liner: Navigates UAVs from language with a reversible cruise-precision controller, instruction-conditioned keyframe memory, and a language-grounded landmark graph.
TYPdMlmbBX.problem: A one-way coarse-to-fine controller may switch prematurely to local search and cannot return to cruise, and long flights make it hard to retain useful past views and reason about landmark relations.
TYPdMlmbBX.method: Combines a controller that returns to cruise when the target is estimated farther away, selective keyframe memory retrieving earlier views conditioned on the instruction, and a landmark graph organizing named places to support goal prediction.
TYPdMlmbBX.key_idea: Let the controller revert from precision to cruise mode when the target estimate moves away, supported by retrieved keyframes and a graph of named landmarks.
TYPdMlmbBX.evidence: Evaluation on all three splits of the refined CityNav benchmark against compared methods, with separately retrained ablations of each component.
TYPdMlmbBX.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims the highest success rate and success weighted by path length among compared methods on all three CityNav splits.
TYPdMlmbBX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three components give clear gains in success rate and SPL on CityNav, with separately retrained ablations, and find the reversible mode switch a promising way to recover from premature switching.
TYPdMlmbBX.main_concern: Design choices are not compared against simpler alternatives and the ablations do not isolate the return-to-cruise mechanism, leaving the contribution closer to an engineering integration.

dVgfIdnRgx.one_liner: Uses Chinese-developed censored open-weights LLMs as a natural testbed to evaluate honesty elicitation and lie detection techniques.
dVgfIdnRgx.problem: Honesty elicitation and lie detection are usually evaluated on models artificially trained to lie, which may not resemble naturally occurring dishonesty.
dVgfIdnRgx.method: It evaluates a suite of elicitation and lie-detection techniques on Qwen3 models that produce falsehoods about politically sensitive topics (such as Tiananmen and the COVID-19 outbreak) while sometimes answering correctly, then tests transfer to DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3.5-397B.
dVgfIdnRgx.key_idea: Censorship-trained models that sometimes answer correctly hold knowledge they suppress, giving a natural ground truth for testing elicitation and lie detection.
dVgfIdnRgx.evidence: Honesty elicitation (sampling without a chat template, few-shot prompting, honesty fine-tuning) and lie detection (self-classification prompting, linear probes) on Qwen3 models with transfer to DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3.5-397B; reviewers note a 90-question test set and 10-question dev set.
dVgfIdnRgx.claimed_gains: Sampling without a chat template, few-shot prompting and fine-tuning on generic honesty data most reliably increase truthful responses, self-classification prompting performs near an uncensored-model upper bound, and no technique fully eliminates false responses; no numbers stated.
dVgfIdnRgx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly defined, the censored-model testbed gives useful insight into naturally arising dishonesty, and simple black-box methods transfer to larger models.
dVgfIdnRgx.main_concern: Benchmark reliability: ground truth relies on GPT-family and other LLMs whose own censorship and bias are unverified, and the test set is small (90 questions with a 10-question dev set).

8fcRsgB2gJ.one_liner: Selects among candidate translation revisions by estimated net value, retaining the current translation when no repair is justified.
8fcRsgB2gJ.problem: LLM translation refinement can damage content that is already correct, and stronger initial translations leave fewer beneficial revisions and smaller attainable gains.
8fcRsgB2gJ.method: Formulates repair as maximizing expected bounded improvement under a population degradation budget, whose Lagrangian gives a net-value rule. RCAS generates candidates along multiple repair directions, estimates benefit and degradation without test-time references, and applies the highest positive-net-value repair or keeps the current translation.
8fcRsgB2gJ.key_idea: A Lagrangian net-value rule scores each candidate repair by estimated benefit minus degradation relative to keeping the current translation, which counts as zero value.
8fcRsgB2gJ.evidence: Five WMT test sets, frozen-pool controls, and a blinded audit of 250 executed edits, with revisions generated by Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 per reviews.
8fcRsgB2gJ.claimed_gains: Highest mean COMET among evaluated repair pipelines on four of five datasets; in a blinded audit of 250 edits, 23.2% repair a major error and only 2.0% introduce one.
8fcRsgB2gJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly defined and that separating candidate-pool opportunity from selection regret is a clean framing, supported by human evaluation beyond automatic metrics.
8fcRsgB2gJ.main_concern: Added value over simple QE-based selection is not shown: training-free QE-best beats RCAS on COMET-22 on all five datasets, and ablations show no benefit of net-value scoring over signed gain.

0YxssEdw8A.one_liner: Repeating one contiguous transformer block restricts frozen-model routing to a searchable quadratic family of layer paths.
0YxssEdw8A.problem: Existing test-time layer-routing spaces grow exponentially with depth, making exhaustive evaluation and route learning costly.
0YxssEdw8A.method: BLR repeats one contiguous layer block once, allowing exhaustive per-instance route evaluation. It supports a fixed training-selected block and a learned router trained on dense rewards over all routes.
0YxssEdw8A.key_idea: Restrict test-time routes to one repeated contiguous layer block, then select that block statically or with an input-dependent router.
0YxssEdw8A.evidence: Experiments span six model families and ten reasoning benchmarks, comparing exhaustive route oracles, static blocks, learned routing, and instruction-tuned models.
0YxssEdw8A.claimed_gains: Per-instance oracle gains are +59.1% overall and up to +75.8% on individual tasks.
0YxssEdw8A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the tractable route family, exhaustive oracle measurements, and systematic analysis of block reuse.
0YxssEdw8A.main_concern: Practical gains concentrate on weakly performing base-model baselines and largely disappear for instruction-tuned models.

3UcB5YG58X.one_liner: Synthetic tests and cost-aware candidate selection recursively evolve agent harnesses for different performance and execution-cost budgets.
3UcB5YG58X.problem: Recursive harness improvement can raise task performance while increasing per-task execution cost.
3UcB5YG58X.method: HarnessPro uses specialized agents to diagnose trajectories, plan updates, and implement candidate harnesses evaluated by LLM-generated tests. Normalized weighted squared-distance selection retains lite, medium, and heavy variants for subsequent iterations.
3UcB5YG58X.key_idea: Iteratively synthesize, test, and select harness modifications using weighted performance–cost distances to maintain multiple deployment-budget options.
3UcB5YG58X.evidence: Experiments cover Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench with GPT-5.5/Codex and GLM-5.2/Claude Code, including repeated runs.
3UcB5YG58X.claimed_gains: With GPT-5.5 and Codex, heavy mode averages a 2.0 percentage point pass-rate gain and a 26.1% per-task cost reduction against the strongest prior label-free baseline.
3UcB5YG58X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit performance–cost optimization and multiple budget-specific harnesses address practical deployment needs.
3UcB5YG58X.main_concern: Unreported harness-evolution costs prevent assessment of total savings and the deployment volume needed to break even.

8Qw0UnF1Q9.one_liner: Structured music, motion, and instrument-contact measurements guide multimodal reasoning about forged instrumental performances.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.problem: Face-centric deepfake detectors miss the physical human–instrument–music relationships that govern instrumental sound production.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.method: HIM-DF supplies bidirectional audio and visual forgeries for modality attribution. HIM-CoT converts performance measurements into queries over pretrained multimodal representations, explicitly representing measurement uncertainty and cross-modal temporal discrepancies.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.key_idea: Use structured music, motion, and contact measurements to reason about which modality violates the human–instrument–music production chain.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.evidence: HIM-DF spans 12 instrument categories, with structured-evidence ablations and evaluations on unseen forgery generators.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending deepfake detection to instrumental performances and providing a benchmark of audio and visual inconsistencies.
8Qw0UnF1Q9.main_concern: The evidence does not clearly establish that production-chain reasoning drives classification rather than label-conditioned explanations or synthesis artifacts.

qpLQ0b7YK7.one_liner: Benchmark of 100 enterprise LLM-development coding tasks testing whether LLM agents can modify large repositories for self-improvement.
qpLQ0b7YK7.problem: Code behind LLM training, evaluation, serving, and infrastructure is still designed and debugged by human engineers, and it is unclear whether LLM agents can handle it for recursive self-improvement.
qpLQ0b7YK7.method: RSIBench-Code reconstructs 100 tasks from practical enterprise LLM-development problems across post-training, training infrastructure, serving, evaluation, and agent systems, covering implementation, repair, test writing, controlled experiments, and execution-path alignment. Agents work in repositories of about 1.8 million source lines with up to 150 turns and a 7,200-second budget.
qpLQ0b7YK7.key_idea: Executable tasks reconstructed from real enterprise LLM-development problems, scored by hidden evaluators in containerized environments, force agents to edit code in repositories of about 1.8M lines.
qpLQ0b7YK7.evidence: Agents are run on the 100 tasks with up to 150 turns and a 7,200-second budget; reviewers add that the paper analyzes task scores, resource use, and trajectories, on two public repositories in CPU-based environments.
qpLQ0b7YK7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target problem is relevant and under-served, the task types are broad, and the pipeline (hidden evaluators, containers, released tasks and graders) supports reuse.
qpLQ0b7YK7.main_concern: Fairness and validity gaps: DeepSeek V4 Pro is used for task selection and final evaluation, evaluators lack independent validation, and the link from solving these tasks to recursive self-improvement is asserted rather than shown.

VkPUXYLEA9.one_liner: A deterministic test-error equivalent guides private transfer-learning dataset selection using summary statistics and weighted ridge regression.
VkPUXYLEA9.problem: Dataset acquisition decisions must anticipate negative transfer and privacy noise without accessing individual records.
VkPUXYLEA9.method: The paper analyzes high-dimensional weighted ridge regression across heterogeneous sources under label-only or joint feature-label privacy. A deterministic test-error equivalent supports selection of source weights and ridge regularizers.
VkPUXYLEA9.key_idea: Express target risk through source summary statistics, model shifts, regularization, and privacy noise to optimize weighted ridge transfer.
VkPUXYLEA9.evidence: Theoretical risk characterization, simulations, and real-data experiments support risk prediction and dataset selection.
VkPUXYLEA9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical risk characterization linking data heterogeneity and privacy noise to transfer performance.
VkPUXYLEA9.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether sufficiently informative source-specific public statistics are available before acquiring the private data.

3AFQIR1z1k.one_liner: Heat-equation evolution and reverse-process inversion guide diffusion reconstruction of land surface temperature from sparse satellite observations.
3AFQIR1z1k.problem: Sparse satellite observations leave temporal reconstruction underconstrained, while conventional diffusion models lack explicit physical structure.
3AFQIR1z1k.method: PhyDiM evolves a clean temperature field using a heat equation before adding Gaussian noise. Reverse sampling inverts that evolution with Laplacian regularization.
3AFQIR1z1k.key_idea: Embed heat-equation evolution before forward noising and invert it during reverse sampling with spatial Laplacian regularization.
3AFQIR1z1k.evidence: Satellite temperature experiments span multiple regions and years with temporal splits, including comparisons against DDPM.
3AFQIR1z1k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize reconstruction benefits from incorporating physical priors into diffusion and reverse sampling.
3AFQIR1z1k.main_concern: Reviewers question whether heat evolution in diffusion time establishes valid physical temperature dynamics rather than spatial smoothing.

knpUsZ52xJ.one_liner: Skill-guided follow-up questions turn solver disagreements into self-generated supervision for Earth observation vision-language models.
knpUsZ52xJ.problem: Earth observation VLMs depend on annotations, while self-generated supervision can lose reliability and task diversity.
knpUsZ52xJ.method: TerraEvo co-trains Proposer and Solver roles on unlabeled imagery through skill-guided Socratic dialogue. Adaptive rewards, skill balancing, replay, and consistency-based signals guide question generation and Solver learning.
knpUsZ52xJ.key_idea: Use Solver answer disagreements to generate skill-targeted follow-up questions and train both roles with label-free consistency and reasoning rewards.
knpUsZ52xJ.evidence: Experiments use Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct across five remote-sensing benchmarks with component ablations.
knpUsZ52xJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge benchmark improvements and useful component ablations supporting the integrated self-training framework.
knpUsZ52xJ.main_concern: Multiple reviewers warn that answer agreement and heuristic reasoning rewards can reinforce shared factual or visual errors.

vKCJppGol7.one_liner: Affine projection enforces polynomial consistency while neural stencil weights learn prescribed spectral responses on unstructured point clouds.
vKCJppGol7.problem: Mesh-free discretizations rely on heuristic kernels that satisfy consistency constraints without optimizing their spectral response.
vKCJppGol7.method: SpeND maps local point-cloud geometry to discretization weights and projects them onto polynomial moment constraints. Unsupervised training matches exact differentiation of Fourier modes within a chosen wavenumber band.
vKCJppGol7.key_idea: Project predicted stencil weights onto exact polynomial moment constraints, then optimize remaining freedom against Fourier differentiation responses.
vKCJppGol7.evidence: The reviews describe Poisson, Taylor–Green, and Burgers experiments comparing numerical accuracy and efficiency with mesh-free methods.
vKCJppGol7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining exact polynomial consistency with learned spectral optimization.
vKCJppGol7.main_concern: Reviewers find the evaluation insufficient to establish stability and accuracy advantages on general irregular geometries.

DWaNSQa8sQ.one_liner: Markov-kernel perturbations show when separate private intervention reports fail to identify a shared causal response.
DWaNSQa8sQ.problem: Communicating abstract causal quantities does not ensure that private reports identify the joint causal response needed by collaborators.
DWaNSQa8sQ.method: The paper constructs local kernel perturbations that preserve separate intervention reports while changing joint responses. It also characterizes identification under additive separability and known noise distributions.
DWaNSQa8sQ.key_idea: Perturb compatible Markov kernels while preserving separate intervention reports to expose non-identifiability of joint responses.
DWaNSQa8sQ.evidence: Theoretical results establish local non-identifiability under explicit conditions and distinguish identification of mean changes from full kernels.
DWaNSQa8sQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the careful local non-identification construction and its use of Markov kernels.
DWaNSQa8sQ.main_concern: Reviewers question the significance and practical reach of extending known non-identifiability obstacles without a demonstrated application.

IrOp0OneJv.one_liner: Generator eigenpairs from trajectory data define independent transport ODEs that sample reversible diffusions' invariant laws.
IrOp0OneJv.problem: Density- or score-based samplers inherit estimation errors near barriers between metastable states.
IrOp0OneJv.method: BKT estimates generator eigenpairs and expansion coefficients from trajectories and an initial sample. It transports each point using the negative logarithmic gradient of the resulting density-ratio expansion.
IrOp0OneJv.key_idea: Use the backward Kolmogorov spectral expansion of the density ratio to construct a fixed transport velocity for independent particle ODEs.
IrOp0OneJv.evidence: Transport identities and stability analysis accompany synthetic experiments and an alanine dipeptide comparison with LAWGD.
IrOp0OneJv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the spectral transport formulation and theoretical error analysis supported by numerical experiments.
IrOp0OneJv.main_concern: Reviewers question practical scalability beyond structured examples because accurate eigenpairs and representative metastable trajectories may be costly.

ao4xVwZE4E.one_liner: Sampled goal-property queries relabel achieved outcomes without forcing offline policies to satisfy every state coordinate.
ao4xVwZE4E.problem: Using complete achieved states as hindsight goals overconstrains tasks that require only some outcome properties.
ao4xVwZE4E.method: GS-HER pairs each achieved outcome with a sampled query specifying which properties constrain the goal, preserving the learner's objective. Inference-time queries let one checkpoint support different goal specifications.
ao4xVwZE4E.key_idea: Condition hindsight goals on sampled property-selection queries while retaining the original achieved outcomes and learning objectives.
ao4xVwZE4E.evidence: Experiments compare five imitation, contrastive, and value-based learners on state-based OGBench manipulation and PointMaze.
ao4xVwZE4E.claimed_gains: Oracle projections increase mean success from 24.4% to 60.0% across all 25 manipulation comparisons, while GS-HER Random achieves 53.5% and improves all 25 comparisons.
ao4xVwZE4E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value flexible goal specification and evidence that full-state conditioning can overconstrain tasks.
ao4xVwZE4E.main_concern: Reviewers question applicability beyond artificial state-based tasks, particularly how to obtain meaningful goal masks for visual observations.

d1Wx9vkfyl.one_liner: A growth-regularized vision transformer maps canopy height over time using multi-sensor satellite data and sparse GEDI labels.
d1Wx9vkfyl.problem: Static global tree-height maps cannot capture forest growth and disturbances needed for temporal monitoring.
d1Wx9vkfyl.method: ECHOSAT trains a vision transformer for pixel-level temporal regression from multi-sensor imagery. A self-supervised growth loss encourages gradual height increases while allowing abrupt forest-loss declines.
d1Wx9vkfyl.key_idea: Regularize temporal canopy-height predictions with growth curves that allow gradual development and abrupt disturbance-related declines.
d1Wx9vkfyl.evidence: Reviews describe global 10 m maps across seven years and single-year accuracy comparisons on GEDI and NEON airborne lidar data.
d1Wx9vkfyl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value global temporal canopy mapping and ecological growth constraints for learning from sparse height labels.
d1Wx9vkfyl.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find no independent quantitative validation that predicted year-to-year height changes accurately recover forest dynamics.

A6ALQp8ceQ.one_liner: Hopfield cross-modal retrieval and associative template updates enable long-term RGB-event tracking on the FELT benchmark.
A6ALQp8ceQ.problem: Event-camera visual object trackers are evaluated primarily on short-term sequences, leaving performance under long-term appearance variation and target disappearance unclear.
A6ALQp8ceQ.method: The paper introduces the FELT benchmark (1,044 long-term videos with 1.9 million RGB-event frame pairs across 60 target classes and 14 attributes) and AMTTrack, a one-stream tracker that fuses multi-scale RGB and event template-search tokens via a Hopfield retrieval layer while maintaining dynamic templates through associative memory updates.
A6ALQp8ceQ.key_idea: Aggregate multi-scale RGB and event template-search tokens through a Hopfield retrieval layer while dynamically updating templates via associative memory.
A6ALQp8ceQ.evidence: Twenty-three baseline trackers are retrained on FELT, and AMTTrack is evaluated across FELT, FE108, VisEvent, and COESOT.
A6ALQp8ceQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large-scale FELT RGB-event dataset with 23 uniformly evaluated trackers is a useful benchmark contribution and that Hopfield memory aligns with template maintenance.
A6ALQp8ceQ.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient mechanisms and direct evaluation for target re-detection after full occlusion or disappearance, alongside missing module ablations on FELT under the final training setup.

fjx2CKLGUA.one_liner: A constructive δ-approximate decision-tree conversion produces fixed-depth ReLU networks with controlled behavioral disagreement.
fjx2CKLGUA.problem: Decision trees are inconvenient in neural deployment and verification pipelines, while exact neural conversions can grow substantially.
fjx2CKLGUA.method: The paper develops exact decision-tree-to-ReLU constructions and a δ-approximate alternative with fixed depth. The approximate construction relaxes exact equivalence through an explicit geometric agreement guarantee.
fjx2CKLGUA.key_idea: Relaxing exact tree-network equivalence to δ-approximate agreement permits a constructive fixed-depth ReLU encoding.
fjx2CKLGUA.evidence: Formal transformation results accompany evaluations on low-dimensional control tasks, including CartPole, across five source architectures.
fjx2CKLGUA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate clear presentation and formal treatment of exact and approximate tree-to-network conversion.
fjx2CKLGUA.main_concern: The fixed-depth networks remain very large, with insufficient comparisons against exact conversion, pruning, or other compact alternatives.

9NDJoG2GDg.one_liner: Text-prototype and Gaussian class-rank agreement jointly correct predictions and gate online distribution updates.
9NDJoG2GDg.problem: An unlabeled sample can need prediction correction while still being unreliable evidence for future adaptation.
9NDJoG2GDg.method: PACE converts rank displacements between text prototypes and online Gaussian models into a compatibility vector. Its class-level log prior adjusts predictions, while a posterior-weighted gate controls Gaussian update responsibility without encoder training.
9NDJoG2GDg.key_idea: Class-rank displacements yield compatibility scores that separately adjust prediction priors and gate each sample's contribution to online Gaussian statistics.
9NDJoG2GDg.evidence: Evaluation covers 21 datasets and domains with ablations and a separate six-domain held-out assessment.
9NDJoG2GDg.claimed_gains: Under oracle tuning, PACE improves on its rank-free counterpart in all 21 evaluations by an average of +1.09 percentage points (+1.02 with ordinal compatibility alone).
9NDJoG2GDg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it useful to distinguish immediate prediction correction from selective statistical updating without backpropagation.
9NDJoG2GDg.main_concern: Oracle tuning on target labels and unmatched baseline protocols weaken the validity of comparative accuracy claims.

YqRWHU8dGJ.one_liner: Controlled paper rewrites vary linguistic confidence and English-writing features to measure style sensitivity in LLM peer review.
YqRWHU8dGJ.problem: LLM reviewers may respond to linguistic style unrelated to a paper's scientific content.
YqRWHU8dGJ.method: Literature-grounded rewriting instructions produce paper variants with different confidence and native/non-native English features, aiming to preserve scientific content. Multiple LLM reviewers assess the variants.
YqRWHU8dGJ.key_idea: Paired style interventions hold intended scientific content constant while varying confidence markers and English-writing features before LLM review.
YqRWHU8dGJ.evidence: Experiments assess ratings and review content, checking linguistic manipulations, reviewer variance, prompt sensitivity, and interactions between style dimensions.
YqRWHU8dGJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the peer-review reliability question and the controlled design with detailed empirical analyses.
YqRWHU8dGJ.main_concern: Without scores for original papers, asymmetric rewrites cannot distinguish rewarding confident wording from penalizing added hedges.

P3zuKazMzC.one_liner: Validated multiparty protocols generate role contracts enforced through deterministic monitoring, message gating, and scheduling.
P3zuKazMzC.problem: Workflow structure and input-output checks do not prevent agent deadlocks, missed decisions, or premature actions.
P3zuKazMzC.method: ProtoGuard uses an LLM to draft a global protocol, validates it with multiparty session types, and derives role-specific contracts. Runtime monitoring, pre-delivery gating, and protocol-aware scheduling enforce those contracts.
P3zuKazMzC.key_idea: Multiparty-session-type validation projects global protocols into local contracts that deterministically gate messages and schedule eligible agent roles.
P3zuKazMzC.evidence: Component ablations evaluate protocol-governed execution across four tasks and four LLMs.
P3zuKazMzC.claimed_gains: Macro-averaged goal-completion rate rises from 4.1% under role-specific instructions without protocol support to 98.9% under the full configuration.
P3zuKazMzC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical connection between static contracts and runtime enforcement, with informative component ablations.
P3zuKazMzC.main_concern: Missing established workflow and deterministic-state-machine baselines leave the added value of multiparty session types unproven.

WZFICgq18L.one_liner: Task-defined historical targets become shared lag and summary features for relational forecasting models.
WZFICgq18L.problem: Relational forecasting models often underuse entity target history, and frozen evaluation databases can exclude available temporal information.
WZFICgq18L.method: The method reconstructs historical targets from task SQL definitions and adds lagged values or summary statistics to existing predictors. A protocol case study examines information excluded between the test cutoff and prediction timestamp.
WZFICgq18L.key_idea: Evaluating task definitions at historical timestamps reconstructs target histories that become model-agnostic forecasting features.
WZFICgq18L.evidence: RelArena-α experiments evaluate shared history features with TabPFN-Rel, GraphSAGE, and LightGBM using controlled search budgets and five seeds.
WZFICgq18L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple, inexpensive intervention that improves multiple forecasting model families under controlled experiments.
WZFICgq18L.main_concern: Missing comparisons with lags from supplied labels prevent attributing gains specifically to reconstructing additional historical targets.

u6AvpdeaI3.one_liner: Learned hierarchical concepts undergo symbolic dependency repair before compilation into executable robot Behavior Trees.
u6AvpdeaI3.problem: Direct language-model plans leave action dependencies implicit, risking invalid preconditions in long-horizon robotic execution.
u6AvpdeaI3.method: HiBT predicts a task-conditioned hierarchy from goals and symbolic states. Deterministic realization closes domain dependencies and compiles the grounded plan into a Behavior Tree.
u6AvpdeaI3.key_idea: A learned hierarchical interface selects task structure, while symbolic dependency closure makes required preconditions explicit in compiled Behavior Trees.
u6AvpdeaI3.evidence: Experiments cover a 60-instance assembly benchmark with four open-source backbones, LIBERO-Long, LIBERO-Hier, matched controls, and interface ablations.
u6AvpdeaI3.claimed_gains: HiBT solves all 60 assembly tasks with subsecond planning latency and reaches 89.2% final-goal success on LIBERO-Long.
u6AvpdeaI3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the learned-symbolic representation well motivated and appreciate its structured treatment of dependencies and ablations.
u6AvpdeaI3.main_concern: Limited external and classical-planning baselines make the benefits over established planning approaches difficult to assess.

zR1e1cBWw0.one_liner: Global and local encoders associate randomized Wi-Fi probe requests using Information Element bytes and relative order.
zR1e1cBWw0.problem: MAC randomization breaks device association, while wireless measurements used by existing methods can vary across environments.
zR1e1cBWw0.method: GLCR learns self-supervised representations from complete Information Element sequences and adaptively selected subsequences. It combines hierarchical byte-to-element encoding, salience-weighted local aggregation, and context-gated refinement.
zR1e1cBWw0.key_idea: Encode complete and selected Information Element sequences with hierarchical protocol modeling and salience-weighted local features.
zR1e1cBWw0.evidence: Reviews report comparisons with association and self-supervised baselines across four datasets using ACC, NMI, and ARI.
zR1e1cBWw0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of probe association and report promising results from representations based on Information Element content and ordering.
zR1e1cBWw0.main_concern: Reviewers question how much methodological novelty the combination adds beyond existing representation-learning and Wi-Fi clustering techniques.

a5g5D9FQl8.one_liner: Replacing rotary position encoding with additive relative bias changes teacher-gradient conflict in cross-attention feature upsampling.
a5g5D9FQl8.problem: Training feature upsamplers with multiple vision foundation model teachers has not consistently improved transfer to unseen teachers.
a5g5D9FQl8.method: The study swaps positional encoding schemes within NAF while retaining the training setup. It compares multiplicative RoPE with additive relative position biases and analyzes teacher gradients and PCGrad interventions.
a5g5D9FQl8.key_idea: Add a separate relative-position term to attention scores instead of rotating content queries and keys with position.
a5g5D9FQl8.evidence: Controlled NAF positional swaps evaluate Cityscapes, VOC, DAVIS, and unseen vision foundation models, with early teacher-gradient analysis and PCGrad comparisons.
a5g5D9FQl8.claimed_gains: Adding a second teacher causes a 0.83 mIoU drop for RoPE on Cityscapes relative to its best single-teacher baseline.
a5g5D9FQl8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the positional-swap experiments identify a useful architectural choice with measurable Cityscapes improvements at low parameter cost.
a5g5D9FQl8.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate coupling form as the causal explanation because initialization, spatial priors, and attention-dependent gradients also differ.

tQCJ61l3Kq.one_liner: Gradient-flow analysis of jointly learned values and softmax scores explains attention polarization on a constant-target task.
tQCJ61l3Kq.problem: Sparse attention emerges in trained transformers even when the task does not require sparse solutions, and its optimization mechanism remains unclear.
tQCJ61l3Kq.method: The paper reduces a fixed-bias attention task through symmetry to a learnable value matrix multiplied by a softmax vector. It proves one-hot convergence under logistic loss and quantitative polarization bounds under square loss, then studies alternative attention nonlinearities in transformers.
tQCJ61l3Kq.key_idea: Higher attention accelerates value learning, and the resulting value differences draw further attention toward the same positions.
tQCJ61l3Kq.evidence: Gradient-flow proofs cover logistic and square losses in the reduced model, while trained-transformer experiments examine token influence and attention sparsity under different nonlinearities.
tQCJ61l3Kq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the constant-target setting isolates an understandable feedback mechanism between value learning and attention concentration.
tQCJ61l3Kq.main_concern: Special initialization and input-independent targets restrict the theory's relevance to realistic transformer training and attention sinks.

y1TfvG7XLQ.one_liner: Encode multi-scale non-forest graph structure for Graph Transformers via ridge-regularized node magnitude residuals from a forest baseline.
y1TfvG7XLQ.problem: Finite-horizon positional encodings like RRWP in Graph Transformers provide a limited structural interface that can fail to distinguish graphs sharing identical local walk profiles.
y1TfvG7XLQ.method: MagResPE computes a deterministic multi-scale node positional encoding from graph magnitude by measuring the ridge-regularized residual relative to an exact closed-form forest reference, mapping every forest to zero while capturing cycles and redundant geodesics.
y1TfvG7XLQ.key_idea: Subtract the exact closed-form forest magnitude weighting from ridge-regularized graph magnitude across scales to isolate non-tree cyclic structure as a node positional encoding.
y1TfvG7XLQ.evidence: Supported by an all-orders BFS-shell expansion and RRWP separation theorems, plus empirical benchmarks augmenting RRWP on ZINC-12K, PascalVOC-SP, and Peptides-struct.
y1TfvG7XLQ.claimed_gains: On ZINC-12K, augmenting RRWP with MagResPE reduces test MAE from 0.0638 ± 0.0036 to 0.0600 ± 0.0021.
y1TfvG7XLQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mathematical derivations linking forest-normalized graph magnitude to girth, triangles, and BFS-shell expansions are rigorous and clearly analyzed.
y1TfvG7XLQ.main_concern: The forest defect reduces to a degree-weighted shortest-path distance histogram overlapping prior distance encodings, while empirical gains over RRWP are small, statistically non-significant under sign tests, and worse than RRWP when used standalone.

mbKUWCsPd2.one_liner: Smooth rubric-level judge log-probability margins with a Gaussian heat kernel before scalar aggregation in GRPO.
mbKUWCsPd2.problem: Discretizing multi-rubric judge feedback into binary rewards in reinforcement learning discards fine-grained quality distinctions among responses within a group.
mbKUWCsPd2.method: Heat-GRPO applies a nonlinear Gaussian perturbation smoothing (Gaussian CDF) to continuous rubric-level judge margins before vectorized scalar aggregation and group-relative advantage normalization.
mbKUWCsPd2.key_idea: Transform continuous rubric-level judge margins through a Gaussian smoothing kernel before weighted scalar aggregation to preserve within-group ranking distinctions while bounding extreme margins.
mbKUWCsPd2.evidence: Evaluated across six LLMs (Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B, Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Llama-3.1-8B), four multi-rubric benchmarks, three seeds, and multiple LLM judges (including Qwen3.8-27B, gpt-oss-20b, and Gemma-4-31B).
mbKUWCsPd2.claimed_gains: Improves rubric scores by up to 25.0% over the strongest baseline, achieves the highest three-seed mean in 23 of 24 conditions, and reduces advantage computation time by 38.9% and 38.2% relative to GDPO and GD2PO.
mbKUWCsPd2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, computationally efficient, and broadly evaluated across six models, four benchmarks, and multiple external LLM judges.
mbKUWCsPd2.main_concern: The main comparisons give Heat-GRPO continuous judge margins while restricting GRPO/GDPO baselines to binarized verdicts, and omit a standard sigmoid probability baseline or comparison with closely related log-likelihood reward transformations.

LipO1r4a01.one_liner: Condition multi-view radar semantic segmentation on cubical persistence features and supervise foreground connectivity via optimal-transport persistence alignment.
LipO1r4a01.problem: Pixel-wise supervision in multi-view radar semantic segmentation fails to constrain object fragmentation and connectivity errors across sparse range-angle, range-Doppler, and angle-Doppler projections.
LipO1r4a01.method: TopoRadar introduces a DuoPerLay module that computes sublevel and superlevel cubical persistence from multi-view features to condition segmentation representations, paired with an optimal-transport structural consistency loss aligning persistent component summaries between predictions and ground truth per view.
LipO1r4a01.key_idea: Condition multi-view radar features on sublevel and superlevel cubical persistence and align predicted and ground-truth persistent components within each view via unbalanced optimal transport.
LipO1r4a01.evidence: Evaluated on the CARRADA multi-view radar semantic segmentation dataset across range-Doppler and range-angle views with mIoU and topological connectivity metrics.
LipO1r4a01.claimed_gains: On CARRADA, achieves 64.87% range-Doppler mIoU, outperforming published TransRadar and HyperRadar results by 0.97 and 1.07 percentage points.
LipO1r4a01.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating view-specific persistent homology conditioning and component-level supervision is well-motivated for sparse radar projections and reduces topological fragmentation errors.
LipO1r4a01.main_concern: Segmentation mIoU gains are inconsistent across views and classes—trailing TransRadar and MARSS on range-angle mIoU, especially on cyclists—and the mathematical formulation of the sublevel structural loss on binary ground truth is unclear.

bU2sN8Mmbm.one_liner: Reconstruct fleet consensus momentum from asynchronous sparse parameter averages and equalize worker sample counts via accumulate-to-match.
bU2sN8Mmbm.problem: Asynchronous sparse parameter averaging avoids global synchronization barriers in distributed training across slow or heterogeneous networks, but suffers from degraded optimization quality and batch-size noise on slower workers.
bU2sN8Mmbm.method: PACE extracts population-level mean motion from successive sparse parameter averages into a shared consensus-velocity buffer for Nesterov-style updates without extra communication, and uses accumulate-to-match (ATM) so heterogeneous workers step only after processing an equal number of samples.
bU2sN8Mmbm.key_idea: Recover a shared consensus-velocity momentum buffer directly from successive asynchronous sparse parameter averages while equalizing per-step sample counts across heterogeneous workers.
bU2sN8Mmbm.evidence: Evaluated on distributed language model training across heterogeneous hardware and geographically distributed networks alongside convergence analysis for a simplified SGD variant.
bU2sN8Mmbm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extracting fleet-level momentum from existing asynchronous sparse parameter averages at zero extra communication cost is an intuitive, practical design for barrier-free distributed training.
bU2sN8Mmbm.main_concern: There is a mismatch between the claimed identical consensus buffer across workers and the worker-specific echo-cancellation subtraction, theoretical guarantees only cover simplified SGD rather than AdamW, and experiments rely on single runs.

i3Cz8YLmVa.one_liner: Maintain out-of-window LLM history as Gaussian slot beliefs updated in natural-parameter space and fused via precision-weighted product of experts.
i3Cz8YLmVa.problem: Compressed fixed-slot memories for long-context language models store point estimates without tracking evidence certainty, treating well-supported facts and noisy single mentions identically during reads and writes.
i3Cz8YLmVa.method: BeliefMem represents history beyond a frozen sliding-window LLM as diagonal Gaussian slot beliefs, using posterior responsibilities for routing, natural-parameter precision accumulation (with decay-based forgetting) for overwrite resistance, and a precision-weighted product-of-experts readout.
i3Cz8YLmVa.key_idea: Maintain compressed memory slots as diagonal Gaussian beliefs in natural-parameter space so accumulated precision governs overwrite resistance and precision-weighted product-of-experts fusion.
i3Cz8YLmVa.evidence: Evaluated across multiple frozen LLM backbones on a six-task LongBench suite against a paired-seed retrained deterministic point-memory baseline after training on 600 examples in 27 minutes.
i3Cz8YLmVa.claimed_gains: Trained on 600 examples in 27 minutes on one GPU, outperforming evaluated compressed-memory baselines on six-task LongBench.
i3Cz8YLmVa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formulating bounded compressed memory as online probabilistic belief updating is conceptually coherent, lightweight, and supported by controlled comparisons against a deterministic point-memory control.
i3Cz8YLmVa.main_concern: The fixed 256-slot diagonal Gaussian memory creates a compression bottleneck for exact recall and cross-slot reasoning, relies on heuristic variational approximations without calibrated uncertainty validation, and is trained and tested mainly on QA tasks.

6myko8Xk9b.one_liner: Replace group-wise GRPO sampling with single-rollout actor-critic updates and double-side token clipping for asynchronous agentic RL.
6myko8Xk9b.problem: Group-wise sampling in GRPO stalls asynchronous reinforcement learning for long-horizon agentic tasks because updates must wait for the slowest rollout in each prompt group.
6myko8Xk9b.method: Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) uses a single rollout per prompt paired with a learned value critic (using frequent critic updates and frozen attention) and strict double-side token-level importance-sampling clipping to stabilize off-policy asynchronous updates.
6myko8Xk9b.key_idea: Combine single-rollout-per-prompt asynchronous sampling with an actor-critic value baseline and strict double-sided token-level clipping to eliminate group synchronization bottlenecks.
6myko8Xk9b.evidence: Evaluated over 1,000 training steps on agentic coding and mathematical reasoning benchmarks including SWE-Bench Verified, AIME 2025, HMMT, BeyondAIME, and IMOAnswerBench.
6myko8Xk9b.claimed_gains: Trains stably for one thousand steps and outperforms GRPO and its variants on SWE-Bench Verified, BeyondAIME, and IMOAnswerBench.
6myko8Xk9b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliminating group-wise rollout synchronization addresses a real bottleneck in asynchronous long-horizon agentic RL and is supported by informative critic and clipping ablations.
6myko8Xk9b.main_concern: Single-rollout training with a value network is essentially standard actor-critic RL repackaged as a GRPO alternative, and the paper omits critical details on the RL training dataset and decontamination for its benchmark scores.

X1WIOe5bEj.one_liner: Gate federated continual updates of large EEG models using cross-client channel-frequency sketches and a routed parameter memory.
X1WIOe5bEj.problem: Pretrained large EEG models must continually adapt to distributed institutional datasets with varying tasks, montage channels, and recording protocols without catastrophic forgetting.
X1WIOe5bEj.method: BrainNEST encodes client multiscale channel and frequency-band structure into compact sketches, matches cross-client correspondences on the server to gate blockwise aggregation into shared or private state, and stores specialized offsets in a routed parameter memory for initializing future compatible clients.
X1WIOe5bEj.key_idea: Match client channel-and-frequency structural sketches on the server to gate blockwise parameter aggregation and route specialized updates into a reusable parameter memory.
X1WIOe5bEj.evidence: Evaluated on 14 EEG datasets spanning seven brain-computer interface task families across two pretrained backbones (CBraMod and CodeBrain).
X1WIOe5bEj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that federated continual adaptation across heterogeneous EEG setups is an important problem and that BrainNEST shows consistent adaptation and retention gains across 14 datasets and two backbones.
X1WIOe5bEj.main_concern: Ablations remove entire modules along with their memory capacity and regularization without a capacity-matched control, and the normalized dispersion sharing gate mathematically closes whenever only one validated client group exists.

F5jQvWBvu6.one_liner: Combine a two-state Human/LLM Markov transition model with a conformal test martingale for false-alarm-controlled detection and localization.
F5jQvWBvu6.problem: Detecting and localizing LLM-generated segments in mixed human-LLM documents via sentence-level predictions causes high document-level false-alarm rates on purely human-written text.
F5jQvWBvu6.method: CoMa-LD embeds a two-state Human/LLM Markov switching model inside a training-free conformal test martingale, summing evidence over candidate authorship paths to control document-level false alarms and decoding the highest-weight path (via Viterbi) to localize generated spans.
F5jQvWBvu6.key_idea: Integrate a two-state Human/LLM Markov path prior into a sequential conformal test martingale to bound document-level false alarms while localizing machine text via maximum-weight path decoding.
F5jQvWBvu6.evidence: Evaluated across multiple text domains (including WritingPrompts) and synthetic authorship transition patterns against change-point and localization baselines.
F5jQvWBvu6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying document-level conformal false-alarm control with sequence-level authorship localization via a shared Markov model is a principled, training-free formulation.
F5jQvWBvu6.main_concern: Mixed-authorship evaluations rely entirely on synthetic alternating paragraphs that match the two-state Markov assumption rather than realistic human-AI collaborative edits, and localization performance depends heavily on an unablated transition hyperparameter.

dXDhH4PQue.one_liner: Decouple fault and condition features for reliability-weighted domain alignment with class-conditional progressive pseudo-label calibration in bearing diagnosis.
dXDhH4PQue.problem: Cross-condition rolling bearing fault diagnosis under long-tailed fault distributions suffers from unreliable uniform domain alignment and pseudo-label bias toward majority fault classes.
dXDhH4PQue.method: SDDA-CCPC disentangles fault-discriminative and operating-condition representations for sample-level reliability-weighted domain alignment, and calibrates target predictions under long-tailed priors by combining classifier-prototype agreement with progressive within-class pseudo-label selection.
dXDhH4PQue.key_idea: Combine reliability-weighted domain alignment of decoupled fault features with prior-calibrated classifier-prototype agreement and within-class progressive selection to supervise minority target fault classes.
dXDhH4PQue.evidence: Evaluated across six long-tailed unsupervised cross-condition transfer tasks under varying load conditions on the CWRU bearing dataset.
dXDhH4PQue.claimed_gains: Across six long-tailed unsupervised cross-condition transfer tasks, SDDA-CCPC achieves an average Macro-F1 of 0.9206.
dXDhH4PQue.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly addressing sample-level domain transferability and minority-class pseudo-label selection via classifier-prototype agreement targets a clear coupled challenge.
dXDhH4PQue.main_concern: The method uses generic imbalanced domain adaptation components evaluated only on CWRU with an implausibly short 20-point (1.67 ms) signal window and an inverted source-prior adjustment formula that penalizes minority classes.

Ayw7IqyzZV.one_liner: Compress retrieved agent skills into state-conditional continuous prefix tokens and evolve the skill library via a predictive-rate bottleneck.
Ayw7IqyzZV.problem: Injecting retrieved procedural skills as full text into language agents wastes context on steps irrelevant to the current decision state and provides no principled metric for maintaining the skill library.
Ayw7IqyzZV.method: Info-Skill encodes retrieved skills into a fixed number of continuous prefix embeddings via a state-conditional stochastic information bottleneck trained with outcome prediction and a variational rate penalty, and uses held-out predictive gain, rate, redundancy, and paired rollouts to update the skill library.
Ayw7IqyzZV.key_idea: Compress retrieved textual skills into state-conditional continuous prefix embeddings under a variational predictive-rate objective that also scores candidate skills for library maintenance.
Ayw7IqyzZV.evidence: Evaluated on embodied interaction (including ALFWorld), unseen-environment transfer, and contaminated skill-library recovery benchmarks.
Ayw7IqyzZV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that compressing retrieved procedural skills conditioned on the current decision state reduces context length and improves robustness against contaminated skill libraries.
Ayw7IqyzZV.main_concern: Under deterministic top-1 skill retrieval both conditional mutual information terms in the theoretical bottleneck vanish, and ablations do not test the state-conditional compressor without the variational rate loss.

e9AQqd9HnY.one_liner: Learn an online hierarchical RL policy to decide when, how much, and which tokens to prune in frozen Vision Transformers.
e9AQqd9HnY.problem: Most Vision Transformer token-reduction methods rely on fixed layer-wise compression schedules or static offline masks, preventing online input-adaptive decisions on when and how much to prune.
e9AQqd9HnY.method: DORA formulates token pruning in frozen ViTs as a finite-horizon MDP where a lightweight hierarchical actor decides at each eligible block whether to prune, the pruning budget, and token identities, trained with complete-prefix shadow evaluations, a privileged critic, and closed-loop accuracy feedback before deploying with hard deletion and variable-length FlashAttention.
e9AQqd9HnY.key_idea: Train a hierarchical RL actor via complete-prefix shadow evaluations to dynamically select pruning blocks, token budgets, and token indices online for frozen ViTs.
e9AQqd9HnY.evidence: Evaluated end-to-end on ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-A across four frozen ViT backbones (DeiT-Base, ViT-B, ViT-L, DINOv2-B).
e9AQqd9HnY.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-1K with DeiT-Base, reduces FLOPs by 38.4% within 1 percentage point of accuracy loss, and averages 16.7% lower compute across four ViT backbones at matched accuracy.
e9AQqd9HnY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that assigning per-step credit via complete-prefix shadow evaluations is well-designed and that end-to-end throughput measurements accounting for actor and packing overhead across four backbones are thorough.
e9AQqd9HnY.main_concern: The learned block-pruning gate converges to a nearly static four-block schedule per backbone, and the paper lacks a learned static-schedule ablation to prove that online per-image budget adaptivity justifies the RL complexity.

up0Xp7sa3S.one_liner: Augment frozen Video-LLM projectors with Gated DeltaNet local-motion and global-state residual experts trained with JEPA objectives.
up0Xp7sa3S.problem: Standard Video-LLM projectors map frame-level visual features independently into the LLM input space without explicitly modeling local inter-frame motion or long-range state transitions.
up0Xp7sa3S.method: Projector-JEPA keeps the vision encoder, base projector, and LLM frozen while adding two Gated DeltaNet recurrent residual experts—a Local Expert over per-position temporal sequences and a State Expert over spatially pooled frame summaries—supervised by JEPA-inspired local correspondence and masked state reconstruction losses.
up0Xp7sa3S.key_idea: Add two Gated DeltaNet recurrent residual branches to a frozen Video-LLM projector to model per-patch local motion and pooled global state transitions under JEPA auxiliary losses.
up0Xp7sa3S.evidence: Evaluated across seven frozen Video-LLMs from the PLM, VideoLLaMA3, and InternVL3 families on five video understanding benchmarks (35 model-benchmark combinations).
up0Xp7sa3S.claimed_gains: Consistently improves performance across all seven Video-LLMs and five video understanding benchmarks.
up0Xp7sa3S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the plug-and-play residual projector is practical for adapting frozen Video-LLMs and yields consistent improvements across all 35 evaluated model-benchmark pairs.
up0Xp7sa3S.main_concern: The paper omits discussion and experimental comparisons with closely related temporal projectors such as STORM, Vista-LLaMA, and Koala, while the dual-branch design shows only modest gains over the State-only expert.

6gDZakKYdj.one_liner: Detect malicious LLM prompts using a stochastically routed bootstrap ensemble of small attack-specialized classifiers.
6gDZakKYdj.problem: Black-box moderation APIs adapt poorly to evolving LLM prompt attacks, while large white-box LLM judges are computationally expensive to run and retrain when new jailbreaks emerge.
6gDZakKYdj.method: BAGEL (Bootstrap AGgregated Ensemble Layer) trains an ensemble of small 86M-parameter classifiers each specialized on a distinct attack dataset, aggregates predictions at inference from a stochastically sampled subset optionally guided by a learned router, and updates incrementally by adding a single newly fine-tuned classifier.
6gDZakKYdj.key_idea: Aggregate predictions from a routed or stochastically sampled subset of small dataset-specialized classifiers so new prompt attacks only require adding one newly fine-tuned 86M model.
6gDZakKYdj.evidence: Evaluated on a held-out test set constructed from external jailbreak and prompt-injection datasets against larger and black-box guardrail baselines.
6gDZakKYdj.claimed_gains: Updates incrementally for new attacks by fine-tuning and adding a single 86M-parameter classifier to the ensemble.
6gDZakKYdj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that maintaining an incrementally updatable ensemble of small specialized classifiers is a practical, modular approach to evolving prompt attacks.
6gDZakKYdj.main_concern: The supposedly source-disjoint test set overlaps with training sources via composite datasets, computational cost is only reported in parameter counts rather than wall-clock latency, and the detector exhibits a high (~30%) false-positive rate on benign prompts.

coQelb9hye.one_liner: Switch long-video LLM prefill from dense to sparse chunk processing online using internal attention signals and pre-encoding frame filtering.
coQelb9hye.problem: Passive prefill in long-video LLMs uniformly encodes and prefills all video chunks even after sufficient task-relevant visual evidence has already been accumulated early in the stream.
coQelb9hye.method: Evi-Prefill formulates chunk-wise video prefill as a training-free POMDP that filters structurally redundant frames (via SSIM) before visual encoding and monitors internal new-chunk attention mass to dynamically switch subsequent chunks from dense to sparse inference.
coQelb9hye.key_idea: Monitor internal attention allocated to incoming video chunks during chunk-wise prefill to trigger an online transition from dense to sparse token processing alongside pre-encoding frame filtering.
coQelb9hye.evidence: Evaluated on two LLaVA-based video LLM backbones across three long-video understanding benchmarks and combined with existing token-compression methods.
coQelb9hye.claimed_gains: Evaluations over 3 benchmarks achieve 1.5–1.9x speedup without average performance degradation.
coQelb9hye.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training-free active prefill and pre-encoding frame filtering provide practical speedups and compose cleanly with existing token-compression methods.
coQelb9hye.main_concern: The POMDP framing overstates a threshold-based attention heuristic that is only tested on LLaVA backbones, lacks a uniform chunk-sampling control at matched budget, and assumes low current-chunk attention implies low future evidence demand.

JM5PVyzQC4.one_liner: Evolve reusable time-series imputation inductive-bias configurations for downstream forecasting via LLM mutation and utility-weighted Thompson sampling.
JM5PVyzQC4.problem: Minimizing imputation error does not optimize downstream time-series forecasting, while existing forecast-oriented imputation models must be retrained whenever the dataset, missingness pattern, or forecaster changes.
JM5PVyzQC4.method: EvoFIF uses an LLM to extract an initial pool of explicit inductive biases from classical imputation algorithms, evolves configurations via utility-weighted Thompson sampling with LLM-based mutation and crossover, and verifies candidates on downstream forecasting utility, objective alignment, and compute cost.
JM5PVyzQC4.key_idea: Evolve combinations of classical imputation inductive biases using LLM-guided mutation and Thompson sampling scored directly on downstream forecasting loss rather than reconstruction error.
JM5PVyzQC4.evidence: Evaluated across nine multivariate time-series datasets, four missingness patterns, and four forecasting models against seven imputation baselines.
JM5PVyzQC4.claimed_gains: On nine multivariate datasets, four missingness patterns, and four forecasting models, EvoFIF attains the lowest downstream loss and imputes scenarios orders of magnitude faster than baselines using a single reused configuration without retraining.
JM5PVyzQC4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning imputation strategy search with downstream forecasting utility is well-motivated and supported by broad experiments across 36 dataset-pattern-forecaster settings.
JM5PVyzQC4.main_concern: The evaluation omits direct comparisons against existing forecast-oriented time-series imputation (FOTSI) baselines and classical imputation methods, fails to report the LLM evolutionary search cost, and does not hold out datasets during search to support cross-dataset transfer claims.

LUWxhwSbe3.one_liner: Compress streaming video tokens online by splatting incoming frame features into a random-projected bilateral grid.
LUWxhwSbe3.problem: Streaming video MLLMs face unbounded visual token accumulation without access to future temporal boundaries, causing accuracy collapse under aggressive compression.
LUWxhwSbe3.method: BGStream is a training-free streaming compression method grounded in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma that projects visual token features into a low-dimensional guidance space and additively splats each incoming frame's tokens on the fly into a spatiotemporal-semantic bilateral grid.
LUWxhwSbe3.key_idea: Project visual tokens via random projection to construct a low-dimensional bilateral grid and additively splat incoming frame tokens into grid cells online without full-video access.
LUWxhwSbe3.evidence: Supported by theoretical aggregation error bounds via the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma and empirical evaluations across three MLLM backbones on StreamingBench and OVO-Bench against seven compression baselines.
LUWxhwSbe3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that additive online bilateral-grid splatting is a cheap, training-free mechanism well-suited to streaming video that outperforms existing compression baselines at ~5% token retention.
LUWxhwSbe3.main_concern: A simple FIFO-only baseline in the paper's ablations already beats all prior baselines and accounts for nearly all the performance, with the bilateral grid adding only 0.64–0.82 points while its theoretical cell-purity condition fails under the actual grid parameters.

T5VpL9sxOJ.one_liner: Distill a strong agent's VLA intervention experience into a reusable playbook recursively refined with a lightweight agent's execution feedback.
T5VpL9sxOJ.problem: Vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies struggle to diagnose execution failures and adapt online, while running a large frontier VLM agent in the control loop is costly.
T5VpL9sxOJ.method: Recursive Harness Distillation lets a strong agent interact with a frozen VLA (via instruction rewriting, attention steering, and action overrides) to author an intervention playbook for a lightweight agent, then recursively refines the playbook using the lightweight agent's closed-loop execution trajectories without updating model weights.
T5VpL9sxOJ.key_idea: Have a strong VLM agent distill VLA intervention strategies into a textual playbook and iteratively refine it using closed-loop execution rollouts from a lightweight agent.
T5VpL9sxOJ.evidence: Evaluated on real-world robotic manipulation tasks and in simulation on SimplerEnv Bridge with a frozen GR00T VLA policy.
T5VpL9sxOJ.claimed_gains: Improves real-world manipulation success from 37.3% to 64.0%; on SimplerEnv Bridge, raises the light agent to 66.7% versus 41.7% for GR00T-only and raises the strong agent to 79.2%.
T5VpL9sxOJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring VLA intervention strategies from a strong VLM to a cheaper VLM via an iteratively refined text playbook is a practical, low-cost deployment paradigm validated on real and simulated robots.
T5VpL9sxOJ.main_concern: The method combines standard prompting and steering heuristics into a markdown playbook without comparing against existing agent memory or harness baselines (such as ExpeL or Code as Policies) or non-recursive summarization.

LJNtUg0Ukr.one_liner: DNASNet decouples spiking architecture updates from weight backpropagation by using task-conditioned spike timing and entropy mirror ascent.
LJNtUg0Ukr.problem: Differentiable architecture search over temporally unrolled spiking networks incurs high memory and computation costs.
LJNtUg0Ukr.method: Spatio-temporal backpropagation learns shared weights, while an STDP-inspired timing rule updates architectures without architecture-level backpropagation. With states and timing evidence fixed, its utility is a concave temporal-balance potential gradient and normalized updates correspond to entropy mirror ascent.
LJNtUg0Ukr.key_idea: Use task-induced spike timing for node-wise architecture probability updates while reserving temporal backpropagation for shared weights.
LJNtUg0Ukr.evidence: Experiments cover CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, DVS-CIFAR-10, and ImageNet1K, with random-run stability analysis, timing ablations, and a fixed-state theoretical interpretation.
LJNtUg0Ukr.claimed_gains: Compared with bilevel optimization, DNASNet reduces peak search memory by up to 22% and search time by up to 51%.
LJNtUg0Ukr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view decoupling architecture updates from temporal backpropagation as a meaningful way to reduce SNN search overhead.
LJNtUg0Ukr.main_concern: Unmatched architecture parameterizations and training settings prevent clean attribution of accuracy gains to the timing-based update rule.

FB76OmXALO.one_liner: FedCSO-LoRA selects gradient-preserving adapter subspaces and aligns them with a global update reference under heterogeneous client ranks.
FB76OmXALO.problem: Random adapter selection wastes limited client rank budgets, while independently optimized local subspaces can produce poorly aligned federated updates.
FB76OmXALO.method: Each client selects combinations of shared adapter coordinates maximizing retained local factor-gradient energy. Coordination aligns that subspace with a global reference while preserving a prescribed energy fraction, and the server maps client updates into common factor coordinates.
FB76OmXALO.key_idea: Optimize low-rank client subspaces for retained gradient energy, then constrain their alignment toward a global update direction.
FB76OmXALO.evidence: Reviews describe gradient-energy analysis and heterogeneous federated fine-tuning comparisons, including GLUE experiments and local-versus-coordinated basis comparisons.
FB76OmXALO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find gradient-based subspace selection and global coordination principled and well motivated for heterogeneous federated LoRA.
FB76OmXALO.main_concern: A subspace chosen from one initial minibatch may not remain useful during local training, and initial gradient-energy guarantees do not establish sustained optimization quality.

zg05mH5Gts.one_liner: CriPO combines on-policy self-distillation and selective advantage correction to recover missing or suppressed rubric-learning signals.
zg05mH5Gts.problem: Rubric RL misses criteria that no rollout satisfies and can suppress satisfied criteria through scalar reward aggregation.
zg05mH5Gts.method: CriPO applies targeted self-distillation and advantage correction to student-generated trajectories. It addresses unexplored and suppressed criteria without relying on externally guided student rollouts that differ from inference conditions.
zg05mH5Gts.key_idea: Use on-policy self-distillation and criterion-targeted advantage correction on student trajectories to recover signals lost by aggregate rubric rewards.
zg05mH5Gts.evidence: Experiments cover multiple model sizes and in-domain and cross-domain tasks, with component ablations, judge comparisons, and token-selection controls.
zg05mH5Gts.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing unexplored from suppressed criteria and connecting those failure modes to targeted training components.
zg05mH5Gts.main_concern: Reviewers question whether counterfactual-teacher token probabilities reliably localize criterion-specific content rather than formatting or unrelated rewriting differences.

rkpwMfjTvb.one_liner: BAPO segments tool-use behavior and contrasts successful versus failed trajectories to assign extra credit to a selected interval.
rkpwMfjTvb.problem: Trajectory-level rewards fail to distinguish meaningful intermediate progress from interactions that contribute little to task completion.
rkpwMfjTvb.method: BAPO detects distributional shifts in tool-use descriptors to locate candidate behavioral intervals. It scores their association with eventual success and redistributes credit toward the highest-scoring interval without an external reward model.
rkpwMfjTvb.key_idea: Detect tool-behavior boundaries, compare interval descriptors across outcomes, and concentrate additional policy-learning credit on the strongest success-associated interval.
rkpwMfjTvb.evidence: Multi-environment experiments report improvements over GiGPO on ALFWorld at two model sizes and over DAPO on Terminal-Bench.
rkpwMfjTvb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value automatic behavioral credit assignment from interaction traces and terminal outcomes without a learned reward model.
rkpwMfjTvb.main_concern: Reviewers agree that concentrating credit on one success-associated interval can miss multiple necessary stages and does not establish causal task progress.

CtegAlSDQj.one_liner: SafeOT solves a joint occupancy-flow projection to derive safety prices for policy updates with multiple cost constraints.
CtegAlSDQj.problem: Separate per-cost multipliers and scalarized penalties complicate stable control of multiple safety budgets in reinforcement learning.
CtegAlSDQj.method: SafeOT formulates safe policy optimization as a budget-constrained flow problem over a CMDP transition graph. A single multi-constraint projection supplies safety prices to an otherwise largely unchanged policy update.
CtegAlSDQj.key_idea: Project empirical occupancy flow under joint safety budgets and use the resulting prices to weight policy-update safety costs.
CtegAlSDQj.evidence: Evaluations cover 16 Safety-Gymnasium and Bullet-Safety-Gym tasks, with controller ablations, budget variations, and additional seeds.
CtegAlSDQj.claimed_gains: SafeOT's projection takes under 0.2 seconds per update and reduces cumulative constraint violation versus TRPO-Lagrangian by 63% and 70% on the two benchmark suites, respectively.
CtegAlSDQj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize low overhead, joint handling of multiple constraints, and reduced training violations against TRPO-Lagrangian.
CtegAlSDQj.main_concern: Reviewers question the added value of flow-derived prices because simple reactive-switch controls often achieve lower violations and need matched return-violation comparisons.

rb2RbEeV3a.one_liner: Ready2Blend maps requirements into modular soft prompts and regularizes their geometry for inference-time blending with a frozen backbone.
rb2RbEeV3a.problem: Continual alignment must incorporate new requirements without forgetting prior behavior or repeatedly updating the full model.
rb2RbEeV3a.method: AlignFormer converts each requirement into a fixed-length prompt stored in a modular bank while freezing the backbone and prior prompts. Composability regularization transfers semantic relationships between instructions into prompt space for blending and reweighting.
rb2RbEeV3a.key_idea: Store requirement-specific soft prompts and regularize their semantic geometry so weighted prompt combinations express combined alignment preferences.
rb2RbEeV3a.evidence: Experiments examine two continual-alignment settings, retention, weighted personalization, and prompt-aggregation ablations.
rb2RbEeV3a.claimed_gains: Ready2Blend reaches 93.1–98.5% of a joint-training reference with competitive retention and up to 4.3× less training time.
rb2RbEeV3a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value modular compositional prompts as a lightweight approach to continual alignment.
rb2RbEeV3a.main_concern: The necessity and validity of the shared prompt geometry remain unclear without simple prompt-tuning controls and clarification of sequential AlignFormer updates.

wm1lqbE7Rb.one_liner: SAFEMAS compares tool-partitioned agent teams under controlled attacks using deterministic checks of resulting environment state.
wm1lqbE7Rb.problem: Splitting tools across agents may fail to contain malicious inputs and may introduce additional vulnerable communication channels.
wm1lqbE7Rb.method: SAFEMAS compares a single agent with four multi-agent architectures in simulated domains using shared scenarios and attacks. It distinguishes delivery and task outcomes through tool-execution and final-state checks.
wm1lqbE7Rb.key_idea: Hold underlying tasks and payloads across agent architectures and measure attack-induced state changes under different privilege and communication structures.
wm1lqbE7Rb.evidence: The study reports 16,056 runs across four domains, 240 tools, 1,110 scenarios, and three models.
wm1lqbE7Rb.claimed_gains: Shared attack types succeed at 53% versus 48% on orchestrated teams and single agents, while all included orchestrated-team attacks succeed at 62% and tampered orchestrator messages at 82%.
wm1lqbE7Rb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the concrete tool-security question and deterministic outcome evaluation across agent architectures.
wm1lqbE7Rb.main_concern: Reviewers question treating state corruption and unauthorized writes as equivalent to completed downstream harm without distinguishing severity or cascade completion.

Diu1GMQGNl.one_liner: FINCH 2.0 fixes conversation protocols before generation to benchmark financial SQL answering, clarification, and refusal decisions.
Diu1GMQGNl.problem: Text-to-SQL benchmarks do not jointly test conversational complexity, ambiguity, adversarial variants, and whether models should answer, ask, or refuse.
Diu1GMQGNl.method: A seeded planner specifies conversation structure before an LLM writes text across 43 protocols in six series. Automated validation and expert audits support per-turn action and SQL-quality evaluation.
Diu1GMQGNl.key_idea: Predefine conversation structure and action labels before text generation, then evaluate action choice alongside SQL quality.
Diu1GMQGNl.evidence: FINCH 2.0 contains 13,024 conversations over 16 databases, with three open-weight models tested on 2,400 conversations and seven experts auditing sampled turns.
Diu1GMQGNl.claimed_gains: Models achieve refusal recall of 89.5–95.3% but clarification recall of 34.9–57.7%, while SQL quality falls from 0.53–0.57 on easy queries to 0.28–0.33 on hard queries.
Diu1GMQGNl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the auditable construction, protocol-labeled conversational resource, and diagnostic baseline controls.
Diu1GMQGNl.main_concern: Reviewers question whether action labels and linguistic shortcuts establish grounded clarification judgments, given limited targeted validation and strong text-only baselines.

2Tao32zP5t.one_liner: Lazy PSNG combines principal-subspace Newton steps with complementary gradient steps and refreshes curvature after accumulated movement crosses a threshold.
2Tao32zP5t.problem: Large Hessian eigenvalues constrain gradient descent, while full Newton updates can be too expensive in high dimensions.
2Tao32zP5t.method: PSNG takes Newton steps in an approximate leading Hessian eigenspace and gradient steps in its orthogonal complement. Lazy PSNG reuses the subspace and projected Hessian until accumulated step length triggers a refresh.
2Tao32zP5t.key_idea: Apply curvature correction only in the leading eigenspace and reuse curvature estimates until accumulated step length reaches a prescribed threshold.
2Tao32zP5t.evidence: Theory analyzes strongly convex quadratics and locally smooth strongly convex objectives, with synthetic logistic-regression experiments and spectral or refresh-policy ablations.
2Tao32zP5t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of hybrid first- and second-order optimization and the local convergence analysis.
