NRzvIU9FyI.evidence: Controlled data-composition and reciprocal response-transfer experiments are run on class-conditioned flow matching models across CIFAR-10, CINIC-10, DiT, and U-Net architectures.
NRzvIU9FyI.claimed_gains: Replacing repeated same-class background images with distinct images reduces target extraction rate from 80.7% to 18.0%, and the parallel response correction preserves approximately 90% of full-transfer copying effects after target removal.
NRzvIU9FyI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled data-composition experiments and the paired-trajectory reciprocal transfer intervention for isolating causal effects.
NRzvIU9FyI.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments are limited to low-resolution class-conditioned models, that the 90% retention claim needs clearer connection to underlying measurements, and that several terms are poorly defined.

YeAi9Rg38D.one_liner: Trains a VLM with SFT and hierarchical execution-feedback RL to generate editable multi-view DXF mechanical drawings with dimensions.
YeAi9Rg38D.problem: Generating standardized multi-view engineering drawings with native dimension annotations from part images and key dimensions without 3D models still requires manual labor.
YeAi9Rg38D.method: The authors build the DimDraft dataset of 5,233 paired text-image inputs, drawing programs, and reference drawings across nine part categories, and train DraftCoder using SFT followed by GRPO with execution feedback. They introduce the Hierarchical Drawing Consistency Reward (HDCR), which scores geometric measurements and dimensional annotations separately so annotation rewards depend on view and geometric quality.
YeAi9Rg38D.key_idea: Combines executable DXF program generation with a hierarchical execution-feedback reward that gates dimensional annotation rewards on view and geometric quality.
YeAi9Rg38D.evidence: Evaluated on the DimDraft benchmark (5,233 samples, nine categories) with 96 GRPO training samples, comparisons to general-purpose VLMs, and reward component ablations.
YeAi9Rg38D.claimed_gains: Achieves an 86.26% rate of scoreable DXF generation, with GRPO on 96 samples yielding 10.29% and 9.12% relative improvements over SFT in complete annotation matching and layout compliance rates.
YeAi9Rg38D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating dimensioned multi-view engineering drawings is a practical, well-defined task and that the paired dataset is a useful resource.
YeAi9Rg38D.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty, missing comparisons against a flat-weighted reward baseline and task-specific models, and sparse qualitative examples.

0dQfjhhpKY.one_liner: Models stale parameter reads as evaluation graphs and predicts unexecuted graph endpoints from one sequential reference trajectory.
0dQfjhhpKY.problem: Aggregate staleness summaries discard which specific update reads each stale parameter state, hiding how read placement alters finite-horizon adaptation outcomes.
0dQfjhhpKY.method: The authors represent historical parameter reads as parameter-state evaluation graphs and analyze update heterogeneity via exact affine analyses and update-map controls. Using a single sequential reference trajectory, they measure each stale read's finite defect, cache and propagate it through subsequent updates, and use a support-guided reliability selector to choose between two approximations.
0dQfjhhpKY.key_idea: Measures finite defects of stale parameter reads on one sequential reference trajectory and propagates cached defects through subsequent updates to predict endpoints of arbitrary evaluation graphs.
0dQfjhhpKY.evidence: Supported by exact affine theoretical analysis and controlled matched-delay experiments across a family of 2,048 evaluation graphs and non-contiguous causal schedules.
0dQfjhhpKY.claimed_gains: Caching defect quantities yields an 18-19x speedup over per-graph exhaustive execution on 2,048 graphs, and the reliability-guided predictor reduces prediction-stage GPU latency by up to 35.9%.
0dQfjhhpKY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matched-delay experiments and exact affine analysis convincingly isolate the structural effect of assigning stale reads to different updates.
0dQfjhhpKY.main_concern: Reviewers note that performance differences between graphs shrink drastically under joint learning-rate and output calibration, leaving the predictor's practical selection benefit unclear.

la2MV6MkCP.one_liner: Decomposes on-policy distillation into category-level and within-category residual updates, retaining residuals only when optimizer-matched trials reduce category loss.
la2MV6MkCP.problem: Standard token-level on-policy distillation couples semantic category selection with within-category token preferences, allowing noisy within-category supervision to interfere with category-level alignment.
la2MV6MkCP.method: SCS-OPD performs the main update using a category-level distillation objective and then runs an optimizer-matched comparison from the same parameters and optimizer state between a category-only step and a step adding the within-category residual. The residual is retained for a second update only if it reduces post-update category-level loss relative to the category-only step.
la2MV6MkCP.key_idea: Uses optimizer-matched trial steps to selectively retain within-category distillation residuals only when they decrease post-update category-level loss.
la2MV6MkCP.evidence: Evaluated against category-only (F-only) and uniform residual (All-R) baselines on math benchmarks (including MATH500, AIME24, AIME25, AMC23 with Qwen3) across four semantic grouping rules and five residual weights.
la2MV6MkCP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clean chain-rule decomposition and the principled optimizer-matched trial mechanism for selective residual supervision.
la2MV6MkCP.main_concern: Reviewers point out small margins without statistical significance, single-seed ablations, unbudgeted extra training compute from trial steps, and unvalidated aggregate residual updates.

ydh3XsRypN.one_liner: Replaces learned latent sub-goal generation with shortest-path search over a graph of real offline trajectory frames for JEPA planning.
ydh3XsRypN.problem: Hierarchical JEPA macro planners frequently predict unconstrained latent sub-goals that do not correspond to physically realisable states.
ydh3XsRypN.method: Metro-WM builds a graph whose vertices are observed frames from offline demonstrations or random-action trajectories, connecting consecutive states with temporal edges and latent-similar frames across episodes with bridge edges. At test time, it selects reachable sub-goals via shortest-path search over this graph and replans from the current state if the micro planner drifts.
ydh3XsRypN.key_idea: Constructs an offline frame graph stitched with cross-episode bridge edges and runs shortest-path search to retrieve realisable sub-goals for a frozen micro planner.
ydh3XsRypN.evidence: Evaluated on four environments (PushT, Cube, TwoRoom, Reacher) across multiple goal distances (up to d=75) with two micro planners against flat and hierarchical latent planning baselines.
ydh3XsRypN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retrieving real recorded frames addresses unrealisable latent sub-goals without training a macro planner and yields clear long-horizon gains across all four environments.
ydh3XsRypN.main_concern: Reviewers warn that visually similar bridge edges do not guarantee physical reachability or prevent perceptual aliasing, and that the method fails when goals lie outside recorded state coverage.

6IThRKF6vh.one_liner: Conditions spectral time-series transformations on Fourier calendar encodings with separate amplitude rescaling and phase calibration kernels.
6IThRKF6vh.problem: Time-domain forecasting models struggle to preserve periodic strength and temporal alignment, and typically treat periodic calendar cues only as auxiliary input features.
6IThRKF6vh.method: HarMoTC is a spectral forecasting framework that uses Fourier calendar encodings to modulate spectral transformations based on temporal context. Within this conditioned framework, separate temporal kernels perform amplitude rescaling and phase calibration to jointly model periodic structure, context-dependent spectral shifts, and cross-variable dependencies.
6IThRKF6vh.key_idea: Modulates frequency-domain transformations using Fourier calendar encodings paired with separate amplitude-rescaling and phase-calibration temporal kernels.
6IThRKF6vh.evidence: Evaluated on seven real-world multivariate time-series datasets, with component ablations on four datasets and calendar-alignment counterfactual interventions on ETTm1.
6IThRKF6vh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focused calendar-conditioned spectral design and the counterfactual calendar-alignment interventions showing reliance on calendar semantics.
6IThRKF6vh.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the asymmetric real-only modulation and weakly evidenced phase-amplitude decoupling branch, and note that detailed validation is mostly limited to ETTm1.

KHVFV7zIoX.one_liner: Introduces a six-format image-to-code diagram benchmark and formulates target-format selection as an input-dependent model decision.
KHVFV7zIoX.problem: Prior image-to-code diagram generation benchmarks target a single format, ignoring trade-offs in expressivity, code complexity, and compatibility across formats.
KHVFV7zIoX.method: The authors construct UniDiagCode, a six-format benchmark containing 341K real-world rendered image-code pairs and 6.3K hand-drawn sketches, and evaluate vision-language models across formats. They further formulate target-format selection as an input-dependent decision so models choose an appropriate format per diagram rather than generating in a fixed format.
KHVFV7zIoX.key_idea: Trains and evaluates VLMs to dynamically select among six diagram code formats per input image to balance visual fidelity and code length.
KHVFV7zIoX.evidence: Benchmarks proprietary and fine-tuned open VLMs (including Qwen3-8B) on UniDiagCode's 341K rendered pairs and 6.3K sketches, supported by blinded human validation of the visual judge.
KHVFV7zIoX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the comprehensive six-format corpus covering rendered diagrams and sketches and the perspective of treating output format as a model decision.
KHVFV7zIoX.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical necessity and cost savings of adaptive format selection over general formats like SVG or TikZ, noting code length omits latency and image-token costs and structural editability is not directly evaluated.

gcpWySPzvc.one_liner: Introduces Multi-SWT-Bench, an eight-language benchmark of 1,963 instances for evaluating LLM reproduction test generation across ecosystems.
gcpWySPzvc.problem: Existing reproduction test generation benchmarks cover only single programming languages, preventing unified cross-language evaluation of LLM agents.
gcpWySPzvc.method: The authors build Multi-SWT-Bench with 1,963 issue-to-test instances across Python, Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, and C++ using executable fail-to-pass screening. They benchmark LLMs across four harnesses: MSWE-agent, MOpenHands, Codex, and Claude Code.
gcpWySPzvc.key_idea: Curate 1,963 multilingual repository issues across eight programming languages with executable pre-fix failure and post-fix pass verification to benchmark reproduction test generators.
gcpWySPzvc.evidence: Evaluates LLMs with four harnesses (MSWE-agent, MOpenHands, Codex, Claude Code) across eight programming languages (on a 340-instance Lite subset noted in reviews).
gcpWySPzvc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that constructing a multilingual benchmark for executable reproduction test generation with up-to-date models and harnesses is useful.
gcpWySPzvc.main_concern: All empirical model evaluations rely on an undisclosed 340-instance Lite subset (~42.5 instances per language) with inconsistent harness prompts and potential confounding from codebase size and fail-to-pass overfitting.

R6MMnCCP8T.one_liner: Generates query-free adversarial faces by ranking a target-attribute public gallery against a reference across surrogates and composing nearest embeddings.
R6MMnCCP8T.problem: Global approximations of a target attribute class obscure the class representations nearest to a reference identity in face-recognition embedding spaces.
R6MMnCCP8T.method: The method uses accessible face recognition models as surrogates and a public gallery to rank chosen-attribute faces by similarity to the reference embedding. It aggregates surrogate rankings and composes the nearest target-attribute representations into a face that changes race or gender while remaining accepted as the reference identity without querying the target model.
R6MMnCCP8T.key_idea: Rank a target-attribute public gallery by similarity to the reference across surrogate face encoders, aggregate rankings, and compose the nearest embeddings to preserve identity acceptance.
R6MMnCCP8T.evidence: Evaluated across held-out recognition models, two commercial APIs, alternative inverse models, galleries, and independent photos of the same identity, compared against NAFG.
R6MMnCCP8T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the zero-query adversarial face setting is meaningful and the empirical coverage across surrogates, inverse models, and commercial APIs shows strong performance over NAFG.
R6MMnCCP8T.main_concern: The contribution is under-compared against broader face-embedding and adversarial transfer literature (only one baseline, NAFG), and attack success drops sharply on independent photos of the same identity.

2UQFQeS2uq.one_liner: Detects MLLM backdoors black-box by replacing each modality with clean references and flagging abnormally persistent responses.
2UQFQeS2uq.problem: Black-box backdoor detection in multimodal LLMs is difficult because perturbing inputs can alter benign semantics while defenders lack access to weights, logits, or activations.
2UQFQeS2uq.method: B3M2 exploits the modality shortcut phenomenon by keeping one input modality fixed while replacing the other with clean reference inputs, then measuring how strongly the original response persists. Inputs showing abnormally high response persistence under either cross-modal intervention are flagged as backdoored without training or trigger knowledge.
2UQFQeS2uq.key_idea: Independently replace image or text inputs with clean references while holding the other modality fixed, flagging inputs whose generated responses persist abnormally.
2UQFQeS2uq.evidence: Evaluated across nine textual, visual, and bimodal backdoor attacks on LLaVA-1.5-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B over VQA-E.
2UQFQeS2uq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-modal source-preserving intervention is an intuitive, training-free, and practical principle for black-box MLLM backdoor detection.
2UQFQeS2uq.main_concern: All three reviewers question whether response persistence is specific to backdoors, noting that benign image-independent prompts or consistent refusals also persist under modality replacement.

Hs8YuqijHZ.one_liner: Scales looped Mixture-of-Experts beyond two iterations by bounding residual variance, re-injecting input embeddings, and diversifying per-loop routing.
Hs8YuqijHZ.problem: Looped MoE Transformers fail to scale past two iterations under FLOPs-matched budgets because accumulating residual variance destabilizes hidden states and routers collapse onto the same experts.
Hs8YuqijHZ.method: LOOM stabilizes deep recurrence by scaling residual updates to bound variance growth and re-injecting input embeddings at every loop. It diversifies computation across loops via per-loop routing mechanisms and uses segmented backpropagation for training.
Hs8YuqijHZ.key_idea: Scale per-loop residual updates, re-inject input embeddings each iteration, and diversify per-loop MoE routing to prevent hidden-state drift and expert collapse.
Hs8YuqijHZ.evidence: Evaluated via FLOPs-matched comparisons, activation variance analyses, component ablations, and commonsense reasoning benchmarks against unlooped and looped MoE baselines.
Hs8YuqijHZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scaling looped MoE models beyond two loops is timely, clearly motivated, and supported by ablations and segmented backpropagation.
Hs8YuqijHZ.main_concern: The unlooped baseline and MoE configuration are non-standard (shallow with unusually dense expert activation, e.g., 26 of 80 experts), undermining FLOPs-matched comparisons and realism.

5Ho1W0HWXx.one_liner: Selects a small LLM with a probe-aware request router, then probes its prefill hidden states to decide flagship escalation.
5Ho1W0HWXx.problem: LLM routing systems must balance cost and quality across small and flagship models, but probing every candidate model is too expensive while request-only signals miss model-specific failures.
5Ho1W0HWXx.method: Route-then-Probe (RTP) first uses a lightweight request-side router trained with correctness labels and probe scores to pick one small model from a pool. It then runs a calibrated probe on only the selected model's prefill hidden states to estimate failure risk and decide whether to escalate to a flagship model.
5Ho1W0HWXx.key_idea: Train a request-side small-model router jointly with probe scores, then read only the chosen model's prefill hidden states with a calibrated probe to gate flagship escalation.
5Ho1W0HWXx.evidence: Evaluated across eleven datasets against routing and cascading baselines, including ablations on latency and routing components.
5Ho1W0HWXx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating request-side model selection from selective prefill probing is a practical, modular architecture with broad empirical coverage.
5Ho1W0HWXx.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty (combining standard routing and hidden-state probing), unaccounted routing compute costs, and weak justification for the 216-query behavioral fingerprints.

25SasdA7JD.one_liner: Uses paired shared-anchor loss certificates and an independent pilot-plan-certify procedure to power counterfactual fine-tuning audits under nuisance shift.
25SasdA7JD.problem: More generated counterfactual edits or higher predictive consistency do not certify that counterfactual post-training improves generalization over factual training under nuisance shifts.
25SasdA7JD.method: The authors formulate certification via shared-anchor paired loss differences and finite-sample power bounds that separate variance cancellation from anchor-reuse savings. An independent pilot-plan-certify procedure selects audit size, sibling count, estimator, and confidence allocation while accounting for uncertainty in pilot planning moments.
25SasdA7JD.key_idea: Formulate counterfactual gain certification as shared-anchor paired loss differences and size the audit via an independent pilot-plan-certify procedure accounting for moment uncertainty.
25SasdA7JD.evidence: Supported by finite-sample power bounds, controlled simulations across three planning laws (144 pilots, 256 replications each), and a prospective Qwen/ReCoRD finite-catalog audit.
25SasdA7JD.claimed_gains: Across three planning laws, 109 of 144 pilots return feasible plans, and each feasible plan succeeds in all 256 fresh replications.
25SasdA7JD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paired shared-anchor certification framework is theoretically grounded, carefully separates dependence sources, and reports limitations honestly.
25SasdA7JD.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about overly conservative audit budgets, unclear realism of Pearson chi-squared nuisance shifts and finite-catalog ReCoRD sampling, and presentation/notation rigor.

U9Jf6fJTIC.one_liner: Weights lane queries via hard-negative contrastive reliability and reasons over split, merge, and control patterns with a heterogeneous hypergraph.
U9Jf6fJTIC.problem: Query-based 3D lane topology methods propagate false-positive lane queries into spurious links and miss group-level road structures like splits, merges, and multi-lane controls.
U9Jf6fJTIC.method: TopoHG trains lane-query representations with contrastive learning and online hard-negative mining to produce reliability scores that softly weight queries before topology reasoning. It then builds a structure-aware heterogeneous hypergraph over lane and traffic-element queries to model split, merge, and control dependencies.
U9Jf6fJTIC.key_idea: Softly weight lane queries using hard-negative contrastive reliability estimates and pass messages over a type-aware heterogeneous hypergraph aligned with split, merge, and control groups.
U9Jf6fJTIC.evidence: Evaluated with ablations on TopoFG (and multi-view lane topology metrics such as OLS and TOPll referenced in reviews).
U9Jf6fJTIC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that suppressing false-positive lane queries before relation prediction and modeling multi-element road topology are well-motivated.
U9Jf6fJTIC.main_concern: Ablations show the hypergraph module contributes little or hurts detection while most headline gains stem from a front-view image-resolution scaling change.

vdf3GYk3zH.one_liner: Learns expert annotation-pattern clusters from anonymous data via a Bayesian mixed-membership model for cluster-level learning to defer.
vdf3GYk3zH.problem: Standard learning-to-defer routers bind to specific training experts and break when real-world expert pools change via turnover or onboarding.
vdf3GYk3zH.method: L2D-Clusters routes queries to expert clusters rather than individuals, using an LDA-style Bayesian mixed-membership model to learn reusable annotation-pattern components from anonymous annotations. New experts are assigned to clusters using a small set of identified annotations without ground-truth labels.
vdf3GYk3zH.key_idea: Uses a Bayesian mixed-membership model on anonymous annotations to learn reusable expert clusters and routes deferral at the cluster level for dynamic expert pools.
vdf3GYk3zH.evidence: Evaluated on three datasets (including synthetic experts and three real pathologists on Chaoyang) covering expert departure, onboarding, and 100 simulated experts.
vdf3GYk3zH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize dynamic expert turnover as a practical L2D limitation and value decoupling the router from individual expert identities using anonymous data.
vdf3GYk3zH.main_concern: Reviewers highlight internal inconsistency and non-identifiability in mixing annotators within minibatches, heavy reliance on synthetic error-rate experts (with near-uniform clusters on real Chaoyang pathologists), and limited novelty beyond LDA.

3NSRuL0BnK.one_liner: Continuously reweights token-level on-policy distillation updates using trajectory outcome agreement and teacher-student disagreement.
3NSRuL0BnK.problem: Standard on-policy distillation weights all token-level teacher corrections uniformly, which can suppress viable student strategies or reinforce unexecutable paths.
3NSRuL0BnK.method: Reward-Aligned Reweighting for On-Policy Distillation (R2-OPD) continuously reallocates teacher supervision weights based on verified trajectory outcome agreement and the magnitude of teacher-student disagreement, preserving dense feedback without extra model passes or value estimators.
3NSRuL0BnK.key_idea: Reallocates token-level on-policy distillation weights continuously using verified trajectory outcome agreement and teacher-student disagreement magnitude.
3NSRuL0BnK.evidence: Evaluated across seven math benchmarks (with three seeds at 1.7B) and LiveCodeBench, alongside first-order theoretical analysis of preference-value misalignment.
3NSRuL0BnK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, overhead-free implementation, careful first-order theoretical analysis, and consistent three-seed 1.7B gains over standard OPD.
3NSRuL0BnK.main_concern: Reviewers note confounded ablations that fail to isolate continuous weighting from simpler outcome-gated baselines (OPDVR, SG-OPD), truncated 3-of-7 benchmark reporting in Table 3, and missing checkpoint-selection details.

CBPEC3Kbtv.one_liner: Quantizes VLMs to W4A4 using hierarchical cross-modal orthogonal transforms and quantization-aware weight channel grouping.
CBPEC3Kbtv.problem: Low-bit post-training quantization of vision-language models suffers severe degradation from heterogeneous, partially overlapping text and vision activation outliers.
CBPEC3Kbtv.method: COTQuant combines Cross-Modal Transform (CMT), which redistributes text and vision activation outliers via output-preserving hierarchical orthogonal transforms, with Quantization-Aware Group Search (QAS), which reorganizes weight channels to minimize group-wise quantization error.
CBPEC3Kbtv.key_idea: Applies output-preserving hierarchical cross-modal orthogonal rotations for activation outliers alongside quantization-aware weight channel grouping.
CBPEC3Kbtv.evidence: Evaluated on three Qwen-family VLMs (up to Qwen3.5-122B) across five multimodal benchmarks under W4A4 quantization, with throughput and memory measurements on Qwen2-VL-7B.
CBPEC3Kbtv.claimed_gains: Retains 98.03%–98.73% of BF16 performance under W4A4 quantization across three VLMs and five benchmarks, including 4-bit PTQ on Qwen3.5-122B.
CBPEC3Kbtv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the observation of partially overlapping cross-modal outlier channels and strong W4A4 accuracy across scales up to 122B.
CBPEC3Kbtv.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons with recent VLM quantization methods (MBQ, MQuant, SplitQ), evaluation restricted to Qwen-family models, unisolated overlap-awareness ablations, and efficiency measurements only at 7B.

Fiuq2wls5v.one_liner: Allocates mixed-precision quantization bit-widths greedily using a solver-free separable layerwise local error score.
Fiuq2wls5v.problem: Mixed-precision post-training quantization faces combinatorial bit-allocation complexity and sensitivity to small or corrupted calibration datasets.
Fiuq2wls5v.method: The authors derive a layerwise probabilistic quantization-error analysis separating propagated and local perturbations, then use a separable local mean-plus-dispersion score in a solver-free greedy allocation algorithm reusable across memory budgets.
Fiuq2wls5v.key_idea: Separates local from propagated quantization error to construct a reusable, solver-free greedy bit-width allocation score.
Fiuq2wls5v.evidence: Evaluated on image denoising with DRUNet at 4-bit average weight budget (clean and corrupted calibration), BSDS500 replication, and quantized diffusion models.
Fiuq2wls5v.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 7.5 dB PSNR gain under corrupted calibration and 28x–2,570x bit-allocation speed-ups over studied baselines on 4-bit DRUNet.
Fiuq2wls5v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the fast, solver-free reusable allocation and stable performance under corrupted calibration with matched controls.
Fiuq2wls5v.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between the theoretical error recursion and the simplified local heuristic, lack of mean-only score ablations to verify the probabilistic robustness claim, and evaluation limited to random masking and weight-only denoising.

CFCTRI36bM.one_liner: Routes tasks across unreliable heterogeneous agent pools via online task-geometry encoding and calibrated weak peer evaluations.
CFCTRI36bM.problem: Orchestrating open pools of heterogeneous AI and human nodes is difficult because internal quality is hidden and profiles or feedback can be deceptive.
CFCTRI36bM.method: HICS learns task geometry online with a task encoder, maintains task-conditioned rolling quality expectations plus direct contextual estimates, and separates answering from evaluation roles to gather dense weak supervision calibrated by reference feedback and audit anchors.
CFCTRI36bM.key_idea: Combines online task-geometry encoding with rolling task-conditioned quality estimates and audit-calibrated peer evaluations to route tasks across unreliable nodes.
CFCTRI36bM.evidence: Evaluated on a MedAgentBoard-based semi-synthetic medical benchmark using prompted GPT-5.5 nodes and controlled simulations with misleading profiles.
CFCTRI36bM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view joint task-conditioned agent quality and evaluator reliability modeling for open heterogeneous node pools as an interesting direction.
CFCTRI36bM.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments use only prompted GPT-5.5 instances (no real human or multi-model nodes), HICS uses 2,640 extra evaluation calls compared to LinUCB, and the writing is hard to parse.

zK9Auofkn0.one_liner: Predicts post-acquisition spatial Pathology Belief updates before scanning to guide sequential multisequence brain MRI acquisition.
zK9Auofkn0.problem: Active information acquisition requires anticipating how an unobserved candidate scan will update the observer's spatial task belief before paying the acquisition cost.
zK9Auofkn0.method: NeuroBelief encodes observed MRI sequences into a spatial Pathology Belief with a frozen encoder and trains a transition model to predict the updated Pathology Belief for any candidate sequence without seeing the image. These predicted transitions drive greedy sequential MRI acquisition.
zK9Auofkn0.key_idea: Predicts how an unobserved candidate MRI sequence will update a frozen encoder's spatial Pathology Belief to drive sequential scan acquisition.
zK9Auofkn0.evidence: Evaluated on BraTS 2023 (internal) and BraTS Africa (external) with withheld-transition compositional generalization and closed-loop acquisition controls.
zK9Auofkn0.claimed_gains: Reduces acquired MRI sequences by 48.4% internally and 44.7% externally relative to four-sequence scanning, with mean Dice 0.68 and 1.41 percentage points below the four-sequence reference.
zK9Auofkn0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean predict-then-verify observer-centric world-model formulation and careful withheld-transition and external evaluation controls.
zK9Auofkn0.main_concern: Reviewers note that the adaptive policy picks the same T1c-to-FLAIR sequence in 91% of internal cases (matching a fixed two-sequence protocol), lacks uncertainty modeling and direct Dice-gain baselines, and omits worst-case patient drops.

uexiiZCgsv.one_liner: Encodes causal conditional-independence repair as minimum-cost Answer Set Programming optimization with contestable redress guarantees.
uexiiZCgsv.problem: Finite-sample conditional-independence tests in constraint-based causal discovery often conflict, and Causal ABA repairs them heuristically without formal user-contestation redress.
uexiiZCgsv.method: OptABA-PC formulates conditional-independence fact repair as a minimum-cost correction problem in Answer Set Programming (ASP) with a compact causal-consistency encoding. It proves a two-way projection correspondence between optimal stable models and minimum-cost correction sets, yielding conflict witnesses and guaranteed redress under user contestations.
uexiiZCgsv.key_idea: Encodes causal consistency in Answer Set Programming so optimal stable models correspond to minimum-cost conditional-independence correction sets with conflict certificates.
uexiiZCgsv.evidence: Provides soundness, completeness, and redress proofs alongside empirical evaluations comparing OptABA-PC against ABA-PC and ASPCR-DAG on small causal graphs.
uexiiZCgsv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean, formal inspectable repair object, conflict certificates, and guaranteed user-contestation semantics.
uexiiZCgsv.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to prior weighted CI-violation optimization and ASP Bayes-Ball encodings (Hyttinen et al. 2014/2017, Borboudakis & Tsamardinos 2016) and note small graph scales and unmatched ASPCR comparison inputs.

xKeCQ0g9QP.one_liner: Benchmarks hierarchical UAV active perception from aerial EQA to viewpoint planning and 5-DoF control with a closed-loop agent.
xKeCQ0g9QP.problem: Aerial embodied perception benchmarks lack aligned evaluation connecting high-level question answering, observation planning, and low-level physical UAV control.
xKeCQ0g9QP.method: ActiveFly-Bench decomposes aerial active perception into Aerial Embodied Question Answering (Air-EQA), Observation Behavior Planning (OBP), and Fine-grained Language-guided UAV Control (FLUC) using simulated and real outdoor trajectories with 5-DoF actions. The authors also build ActiveFly, a closed-loop UAV agent deployed on a physical drone.
xKeCQ0g9QP.key_idea: Aligns Air-EQA, observation behavior planning, and 5-DoF UAV/gimbal control supervision across simulated and real outdoor trajectories.
xKeCQ0g9QP.evidence: Evaluated representative VLMs, VLA models, and ActiveFly across 10k simulated and real outdoor trajectories and physical UAV deployment.
xKeCQ0g9QP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the aligned three-level decomposition covering QA, viewpoint planning, and 5-DoF flight/gimbal control in both simulation and real-world UAV tests.
xKeCQ0g9QP.main_concern: Reviewers note substantial overlap with CityEQA, UAV-Flow, and EXPRESS-Bench, conflation of planning ability with trajectory annotations in Table 1, and overly rigid oracle-trajectory end-to-end metrics.

YoJHItTeUl.one_liner: Introduces a closed-loop urban navigation sandbox with localization perturbations and counterfactual tool-vision conflict training.
YoJHItTeUl.problem: Urban navigation systems are evaluated in isolated components and fail when noisy route-guidance tools disagree with egocentric visual observations.
YoJHItTeUl.method: CityLoop unifies online navigation, 2D Gaussian Splatting simulation, and physical robots under controllable pose perturbations. RouteGround trains navigation policies through structured capabilities including counterfactual tool-vision conflicts and full-route execution.
YoJHItTeUl.key_idea: Generates controllable localization-induced tool-vision conflicts in a unified 2DGS urban sandbox and trains policies with counterfactual conflict supervision.
YoJHItTeUl.evidence: Evaluated on 1,000 open-loop routes across 43 cities, 50 closed-loop MatrixCity 2DGS routes, and physical robot tests with sequential ablations.
YoJHItTeUl.claimed_gains: RouteGround improves keypoint decision accuracy over the strongest baseline from 47.6% to 78.4%.
YoJHItTeUl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value unifying request-to-arrival urban navigation under controllable localization perturbations and using counterfactual conflicts to reduce blind tool copying.
YoJHItTeUl.main_concern: Reviewers flag small closed-loop scale (50 routes in one scene), unmatched input modalities across baselines, unclear train/test city disjointness, and non-monotonic perturbation results confounded by route projection.

ZSFKzdJGFP.one_liner: Uses return-to-go from a single action-free cross-embodiment mentor trajectory as a critic baseline in sparse-reward RL.
ZSFKzdJGFP.problem: Online RL agents in sparse-reward tasks struggle to learn when only a single action-free demonstration from a differently embodied mentor is available.
ZSFKzdJGFP.method: Mentor-Baseline Implicit Imitation Learning (MB-I2L) maps states via approximate mentor-observer correspondence, uses the mentor's return-to-go to form state baselines for the observer's critic target, and bounds policy performance loss from mentor-derived baseline optimism.
ZSFKzdJGFP.key_idea: Propagates return-to-go from a single action-free mentor trajectory through approximate state correspondence as a critic baseline for cross-embodiment RL.
ZSFKzdJGFP.evidence: Provides theoretical performance-loss bounds and MuJoCo sparse-reward experiments transferring from a ball mentor to AntMaze and Hopper obstacle-crossing observers.
ZSFKzdJGFP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the cross-embodiment value-transfer mechanism enabling observers to outperform an action-free mentor and the theoretical analysis of baseline optimism.
ZSFKzdJGFP.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on prespecified coordinate correspondences, limited evaluation on simple MuJoCo tasks where body dynamics have minor impact on shared features, and missing closely related implicit-imitation baselines.

PgwqK0EXNl.one_liner: Benchmarks visual difference understanding, evolves a small model's tool harness via a coding agent, and verifies captions agentically.
PgwqK0EXNl.problem: MLLMs struggle to detect fine-grained visual differences between similar images, and open-ended difference captioning lacks grounded, verifiable evaluation.
PgwqK0EXNl.method: VDiff-Bench pairs 1,756 MCQ items across 10 change categories with 300 open-ended generation pairs evaluated by VDiff-Judge, a tool-augmented agentic judge with verifiable traces. Expert-guided Harness Evolution (EHE) uses an expert coding agent and execution traces to iteratively revise tools, routing, and response handling around a frozen small base model.
PgwqK0EXNl.key_idea: Uses an expert coding agent to iteratively evolve a frozen base MLLM's tool harness from failure traces while evaluating open-ended captions with a trace-verifying agentic judge.
PgwqK0EXNl.evidence: Evaluated 12 MLLMs on VDiff-Bench-MCQ (1,756 items) and VDiff-Bench-Gen (300 pairs), plus human agreement validation of VDiff-Judge on 100 samples.
PgwqK0EXNl.claimed_gains: Expert-guided Harness Evolution improves the small base agent's MCQ performance by 26.9%, reaching performance comparable to GPT-5.4.
PgwqK0EXNl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the two-track diagnostic benchmark, concrete failure analysis, and evidence-grounded VDiff-Judge with strong human agreement.
PgwqK0EXNl.main_concern: Reviewers question attribution of EHE gains—noting the initial harness already achieves 80% dev accuracy and only two edits are accepted, largest gains occur on programmatic low-level categories—and flag missing comparisons to Meta-Harness and Self-Harness.

Ngg5l67vYL.one_liner: Pairs reusable construction assets with task-specific rubrics and bounded validation-repair loops to synthesize executable business-automation tasks.
Ngg5l67vYL.problem: Traditional rubric-based task synthesis forces authors to repeatedly recreate application interfaces, initial records, policy evidence, and outcome checks for every task.
Ngg5l67vYL.method: AssetForge combines a library of reusable construction assets (application interfaces, world-state components, policy carriers, and native assertions) with task-specific rubrics that instantiate them. Executable checks and model-based review validate each candidate task and provide feedback for bounded repair before acceptance.
Ngg5l67vYL.key_idea: Decouples reusable application infrastructure and assertion assets from task-specific rubrics, then filters and repairs synthesized tasks through executable and model-based validation.
Ngg5l67vYL.evidence: Evaluated by fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 6,000 synthesized examples with GLM-5.3 supervision on AutomationBench v1.0.6 public-600 and matching cumulative training input tokens against traditional Rubrics.
Ngg5l67vYL.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 6,000 AssetForge examples reaches 41.17% strict pass@1 on AutomationBench v1.0.6 public-600 (4.4x the 9.33% base score, +31.83 points), beating traditional Rubrics (30.33%) by +10.83 points (35.7% relative) and by +10.00 points (40.33% vs. 30.33%) at matched training input tokens.
Ngg5l67vYL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that AssetForge addresses a practical bottleneck in synthesizing verifiable business-automation tasks and shows clear end-to-end gains over the matched-supervisor Rubrics pipeline.
Ngg5l67vYL.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of controlled ablations isolating reusable assets from confounders such as differing rubric text, 37.5% more training tokens (176M vs. 128M), and different trajectory complexity.

4grRy0yzlG.one_liner: Maintains persistent per-memory interference states with suppression dynamics to adapt agent retrieval indices online without altering stored content.
4grRy0yzlG.problem: Retrieval-based agent memory systems modify stored content while leaving the retrieval index fixed, causing retained memories to be missed during deployment.
4grRy0yzlG.method: Adaptive Memory Index Evolution (AMIE) wraps existing memory hosts with a bounded persistent interference state per memory derived from deployment retrieval traffic. It applies suppression dynamics during retrieval to reduce repeated slot competition and updates the index online without modifying stored content or retraining the host.
4grRy0yzlG.key_idea: Tracks per-memory retrieval interference from live queries and applies online suppression dynamics in a wrapper index to curb repeated slot competition.
4grRy0yzlG.evidence: Evaluated across five heterogeneous memory hosts (including BM25, Mem0, and Memory-R2) on retrieval and downstream QA benchmarks (including LoCoMo, GroupMem, and MemBench).
4grRy0yzlG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling persistent retrieval-access state from stored memory content is a clean, practical framing evaluated across five heterogeneous memory systems.
4grRy0yzlG.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological distinction from prior access-strength memory systems, note small effect sizes (often under 2 percentage points), and flag missing reproducibility details and uncertainty estimates.

U0mxQn6E1n.one_liner: Uses Fourier analysis and gradient-flow proofs to show task symmetry forces recurrent networks to learn and retain a total-count feature.
U0mxQn6E1n.problem: It is unclear how symmetries in a task's specification determine which representation a recurrent network selects when multiple feature sets solve the task.
U0mxQn6E1n.method: The authors design a state-tracking task requiring simultaneous tracking of multiple identical counters and analyze the solution space via Fourier analysis. They prove that symmetry-respecting gradient flow initially learns only a total-count feature, explain its persistence in an idealized model, and test three recurrent architectures.
U0mxQn6E1n.key_idea: Symmetry-equivariant gradient flow restricts early learning on identical-counter tracking to an invariant total-count Fourier feature, which persists after symmetry breaking and displaces an individual counter feature.
U0mxQn6E1n.evidence: Supported by Fourier analysis, gradient-flow proofs, an idealized persistence model, and experiments on three recurrent network architectures.
U0mxQn6E1n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question about how task symmetry drives representation selection in recurrent networks is important, clean, and rigorously studied.
U0mxQn6E1n.main_concern: All three reviewers highlight severe writing and structural clarity issues caused by dense formal definitions and disconnected prose that make the paper hard to follow.

4WKV4OfXSX.one_liner: Aligns 18 urban modalities across 16 cities over 26 years into a unified benchmark for cross-modal translation and agentic reasoning.
4WKV4OfXSX.problem: Existing earth observation and urban benchmarks lack unified longitudinal multi-layer data capturing joint changes across infrastructure, human activity, and environment.
4WKV4OfXSX.method: AgenticCity-Bench aligns 18 heterogeneous urban, activity, and environmental modalities across 16 cities in 12 countries from 2000 to 2025 under a common spatial reference and calendar index with provenance and tile-level availability masks. It defines cross-modal translation tasks and agentic reasoning tasks covering forecasting, planning, and resource analysis.
4WKV4OfXSX.key_idea: Registers 18 longitudinal urban and earth-observation modalities onto a shared spatial-temporal grid with availability masks to benchmark cross-modal translation and agentic city tasks.
4WKV4OfXSX.evidence: Covers 16 cities across six continents from 2000 to 2025 with 18 modalities, evaluated on cross-modal translation with four fine-tuned generative models and six agentic tasks.
4WKV4OfXSX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that curating and aligning 18 heterogeneous urban modalities across 16 cities and 26 years is a substantial and useful data resource.
4WKV4OfXSX.main_concern: Reviewers note severe modality availability imbalances, geographic bias in agentic tasks, and weak task difficulty where simple baselines rival agents and planning reduces to classification.

gxl2QFxDfu.one_liner: Trains autoregressive Boltzmann generators conditioned on text and coordinate prefixes without atom-wise molecular encoders.
gxl2QFxDfu.problem: Existing Boltzmann generators typically specialize to single molecules or specific molecular classes and rely on specialized molecular encoders that limit transferability.
gxl2QFxDfu.method: Prefix-Conditioned Boltzmann Generators (PBGs) formulate autoregressive Boltzmann sampling over discretized coordinates conditioned on text and coordinate prefixes without a dedicated atom-wise encoder. The authors map scaling laws over model size, tokens, compute, atom count, and discretization resolution on Many Peptides and scale PBGs up to 640M parameters.
gxl2QFxDfu.key_idea: Replaces specialized atom-wise encoders with text-and-coordinate prefix conditioning in discretized autoregressive transformers to enable tractable-likelihood Boltzmann sampling across chemical systems.
gxl2QFxDfu.evidence: Trained and scaled up to 640M parameters on Many Peptides (unseen peptides up to 157 atoms) and tested on small-molecule sampling, solvation free energy estimation, and microsolvation over 280 atoms.
gxl2QFxDfu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the systematic scaling and discretization analysis, clear writing, and strong Many Peptides results from the 640M-parameter model.
gxl2QFxDfu.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that prefix conditioning is never ablated against graph/encoder conditioning at matched model size, optimizer, and token budget, and sampling quality still degrades steeply with atom count.

XzNp808k7s.one_liner: Maps source-model refusal and harm-detection directions into target LLMs via depth-interpolated linear bridges for localized activation-steering jailbreaks.
XzNp808k7s.problem: White-box safety auditing extracts refusal directions from the target model alone, potentially missing vulnerabilities exposed by directions learned in other models.
XzNp808k7s.method: COMBAT extracts banks of refusal and harm-detection directions from a source LLM and projects them into a target LLM's hidden space using depth-interpolated bridges handling unequal depths. It runs constrained two-phase configuration selection and applies localized steering interventions with a triangular layer taper.
XzNp808k7s.key_idea: Transfers source-model refusal and harm-detection vectors across unequal-depth LLMs via depth-interpolated linear bridges and deploys them with two-phase selected triangular-tapered steering.
XzNp808k7s.evidence: Evaluated across 20 ordered source-target pairs from five aligned LLMs on four primary safety benchmarks (18,925 paired evaluations) against equal-budget target-native controls.
XzNp808k7s.claimed_gains: Across four primary benchmarks, Full COMBAT achieves 96.2% micro-average GPT-judged attack success rate versus 88.7% for the equal-budget target-native control and 20.3% for unmodified targets, exposing 1,156 unique failures across 18,925 paired evaluations.
XzNp808k7s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-model transfer of safety directions is an interesting question and that COMBAT achieves strong attack success rates across all 20 source-target pairs.
XzNp808k7s.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical threat model since white-box target access is already required, note limited novelty beyond combining existing components, and flag missing white-box baselines like GCG.

OYmUc7rVtd.one_liner: Refines coarse Mel or codec audio reconstructions in the complex STFT domain using restoration bridges and multi-NFE adversarial fine-tuning.
OYmUc7rVtd.problem: Reconstructing high-fidelity audio from Mel spectrograms or low-bitrate neural codecs is underdetermined and often requires slow iterative sampling or separate models per step budget.
OYmUc7rVtd.method: ReVoC starts from a cheap Mel-inversion or native codec-decoded estimate and refines it in the complex STFT domain with a Vocos-style 1D backbone via restoration bridges. Multi-NFE adversarial fine-tuning uses a step-conditioned discriminator to jointly optimize 1-, 2-, and 4-step inference trajectories in one generator.
OYmUc7rVtd.key_idea: Refine coarse inverted or decoded waveforms in complex STFT space via restoration bridges jointly fine-tuned across 1-, 2-, and 4-step budgets with a step-conditioned GAN discriminator.
OYmUc7rVtd.evidence: Evaluated on Mel-conditioned vocoding (compared to Vocos and BridgeVoC) and neural codec restoration for EnCodec (3 and 6 kbps) and Mimi (1.1 kbps).
OYmUc7rVtd.claimed_gains: On Mel vocoding, ReVoC-Small improves one-step PESQ from 3.592 to 4.142 over Vocos, and four-step ReVoC-Base reaches 4.433 PESQ with roughly 4x the GPU throughput of four-step BridgeVoC.
OYmUc7rVtd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint multi-NFE training cleanly supports multiple step budgets in a single efficient generator and improves objective speech metrics.
OYmUc7rVtd.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over existing bridge and GAN audio methods, lack of evaluation on TTS-predicted Mel spectrograms or fullband/non-speech audio, and weak or unmatched baselines.

HYMwikN0Sr.one_liner: Reranks retrieved Text-to-SQL demonstrations using a literal-abstracted bi-encoder trained with candidate-aware contrastive negatives.
HYMwikN0Sr.problem: Semantic or schema-similarity retrievers in Text-to-SQL often miss structurally relevant SQL demonstrations from the Top-K prompt context, creating a demonstration exposure bottleneck.
HYMwikN0Sr.method: SARank starts from a schema-aware candidate pool, masks SQL literals, and trains a shared encoder with a candidate-aware contrastive loss combining retrieval-based, same-database, and random negatives to score question-SQL structural compatibility without target SQL prediction or execution feedback.
HYMwikN0Sr.key_idea: Abstract SQL literals and train a shared contrastive reranker with retrieval-based, same-database, and random negatives to reorder candidate demonstrations by structural compatibility.
HYMwikN0Sr.evidence: Evaluated across Spider, BIRD, BEAVER, and Dr.Spider with multiple LLMs, plus masking, negative-sampling, and candidate-budget ablations.
HYMwikN0Sr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SARank targets a concrete Top-K exposure bottleneck, isolates reranking cleanly with fixed prompts and pools, and improves structural retrieval and execution accuracy.
HYMwikN0Sr.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty, missing controlled comparisons against structure-aware selectors (like ASTReS) and an untuned matched backbone, and under-specified training/evaluation splits.

DQ8gS7iPfK.one_liner: Injects cascaded Retinex illumination/reflectance priors and foundation-model features into targeted U-Net stages via prior-specific fusion modules.
DQ8gS7iPfK.problem: Low-light image enhancement methods typically rely on a single prior or fuse multiple visual priors uniformly, underutilizing complementary physical and semantic cues.
DQ8gS7iPfK.method: RePriFusion uses a cascaded Retinex estimator to extract illumination and reflectance features and an intermediate reconstruction, then injects those priors plus frozen vision foundation model features into selected U-Net stages via dedicated fusion operators, trained with mixed-dataset sampling and noise augmentation.
DQ8gS7iPfK.key_idea: Pair a cascaded Retinex estimator with role-specific fusion operators that inject illumination, reflectance, and foundation-model priors into distinct U-Net stages.
DQ8gS7iPfK.evidence: Evaluated on five paired low-light image enhancement benchmarks and eight unseen zero-shot datasets, with extensive ablations over priors, stages, operators, losses, and augmentations.
DQ8gS7iPfK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the comprehensive, well-controlled ablation studies and strong empirical performance across paired and unseen benchmarks.
DQ8gS7iPfK.main_concern: Reviewers consider the method an incremental engineering combination of Retinex and foundation-model priors, noting marginal (~0.1 dB) gains over uniform fusion and no explicit decomposition loss ensuring physical Retinex semantics.

TUvvpmE7PN.one_liner: Evaluates video-LLMs on physical anomalies across four progressive tasks using an Ontological-Causal taxonomy and generator-matched controls.
TUvvpmE7PN.problem: Existing physical-anomaly video benchmarks rely on coarse binary checks or real-versus-generated splits that confound physical understanding with visual artifact detection.
TUvvpmE7PN.method: Video-HOCA organizes visible physical violations into an Ontological-Causal taxonomy and evaluates plausibility judgment, category attribution, fine-grained recognition, and mechanism explanation on 1,439+ videos and 3,470 QA pairs, plus 250 generator-matched normal/anomalous control pairs.
TUvvpmE7PN.key_idea: Evaluate four progressive anomaly-reasoning tasks on a shared Ontological-Causal video set alongside a same-generator control split to separate physics understanding from source detection.
TUvvpmE7PN.evidence: Evaluated 20 Instruct-mode video-LLMs on the main benchmark and 17 open-weight models on the matched-generator control, with frame-shuffling, annotation agreement, and judge-sensitivity analyses.
TUvvpmE7PN.claimed_gains: Across 20 models, mean Ontological/Causal nine-way macro-F1 is 37.9/46.0; on the matched-generator control, mean plausibility accuracy of 17 open-weight models drops from 74.0% to 64.4% and the top model on the original split becomes the worst.
TUvvpmE7PN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the structured four-task diagnostic hierarchy and the generator-matched control revealing source-detection shortcuts in real-versus-generated splits.
TUvvpmE7PN.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the small core dataset (630 videos mostly reused from prior benchmarks), undocumented human baseline methodology, and inconsistencies in judge prompts and label boundaries.
